This dark staff features a dragon coiling around a gemstone at its top. A wisp of smoke drifts from the dragon's mouth. While holding this staff, you have advantage on any saving throw against an effect created by a dragon. In addition, while a wyrmling is summoned by the staff, you have resistance to the damage type the wyrmling is immune to.

Summon Wyrmling

While holding the staff, you can use an action to summon a dragon wyrmling in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. The wyrmling can be any kind of chromatic or metallic dragon of your choice, but once a wyrmling has been summoned, that kind of dragon wyrmling can't be summoned by the staff again until the next dawn.

The wyrmling is friendly to you and your companions for the duration. In combat, the wyrmling shares your initiative count, but takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any commands to the wyrmling, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes no actions.

The wyrmling disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or after 1 hour. It disappears early if you use an action to dismiss the wyrmling or summon another one. The wyrmling uses your spell attack bonus and spell save DC for its attacks and breath weapons, respectively. Whenever the wyrmling uses its breath weapon, you can choose for the effect to simultaneously originate from both the wyrmling and the end of the staff (no action required by you), provided you're holding the staff. A target in the area of both instances of the breath weapon is affected only once.

When you draw a sword from this magic scabbard, you can choose to speak its command word to coat the sword in a special poison (no action required). The first creature hit with that weapon within 1 minute must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 4d6 poison damage and is poisoned until the end of its next turn. On a success, the creature takes half as much poison damage and isn't poisoned. Once the scabbard is used to coat a sword in this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

This clay coin bears a sculpted xorn eye at its center, and is usually found in a small leaden box. While holding the coin, you can use an action to speak its command word to animate the eye. The eye remains animated for 10 minutes. For the duration, the eye swivels to face the nearest gem or piece of precious metal within 60 feet of it that's worth 10 gp or more, provided the object isn't being worn or carried. This effect can penetrate most barriers, but it is blocked by 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

This special cocktail shaker allows magic to mix homogeneously into the drinks within. If you mix two potions together in this way and roll on a table to determine the outcome (such as the Potion Miscibility table), you can roll on the table twice and use either result.

While you're mixing a drink in this shaker, you can use an action to expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher. When you do, roll on the table below to randomly determine what effect is imbued in the drink; you can choose the effect instead if you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher. The effect lasts for 1 hour. Regardless of the effect, the drink becomes magical: if the drink is alcoholic, its alcohol affects a creature twice as much as the alcohol within a nonmagical beverage.

When you make an ability check using a skill with which you aren't proficient while wearing this amulet, you can reroll the check if you roll a 1 or 2 on the d20. You must use the new roll. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

This rod is a strange device from a far-flung age and can sometimes be found in the lairs of sphinxes that have traveled through time. The rod has two halves with markings along their edge. You can use a bonus action to twist the two halves to align the markings in one the four ways detailed below.

Barrier

The rod emits a magical shield from it, allowing you to wield it by holding the rod. Treat it as a +2 shield. Whenever a creature makes a melee attack against you while you're holding the shield, that creature takes 2 lightning damage.

Baton

The rod emits a magical baton from its end. Treat the baton as a +2 club, except it uses a d8 damage die and deals lightning damage instead of bludgeoning. If you hit a creature with the baton and roll a 8 on the damage die, the target can't make opportunity attacks until the end of your next turn.

Blaster

The rod emits a magical blast of electricity from its end. Treat the blaster as a +2 light crossbow, except it doesn't have the two-handed or loading properties, creates its own ammunition, and uses a d6 damage die and deals lightning damage instead of piercing. If you hit a creature with the blaster and roll an 6 on the damage die, the target can't make opportunity attacks until the end of your next turn.

Off

The rod is turned off, preventing it from using any time from its power source until the rod's halves are switched to a different option.

The rod runs on a power source that's fueled by magic. The rod can be used for up to 4 hours before the power source is empty. Deduct the time you use it in increments of 10 minutes from the power source's total time. You know how much remaining time the source has while holding the rod. Any creature can use an action to expend a spell slot level of 1st level or higher into the power source, adding to its total remaining time, by touching the rod as the spell slot is expended. The power source regains a number of hours of power equal to the spell slot level that was expended into it. When found, the rod has 1d4 hours of power remaining, and it can't have more than 4 hours at a time.

Overcharge

Once per turn when you deal lightning damage to a creature using the rod, you can deduct 2 hours of time from its power source to force that creature to make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is stunned until the end of your next turn.

While wearing this ring, you can use a bonus action to summon a mundane melee weapon of your choice to the hand that's wearing it, such as a handaxe, scimitar, or whip. The weapon can't have the two-handed or special property, and it immediately vanishes if it's no longer in your hand, if you summon another weapon in this way, or if you're no longer wearing the ring. The weapon is considered magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

This wooden staff cradles a translucent orb at its top. While attuned to this staff, you have proficiency in the Medicine skill, and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it. This staff can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.

The staff has 16 charges for the following properties. It regains 2d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you roll a 1 on both d6s, the staff regains all expended charges.

Spells

While holding the staff, you can expend some of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using the spell's normal casting time and your spell attack bonus and spellcasting ability modifier: acid arrow (2 charges), cure wounds (1 charge per spell level, up to 9th), death ward (4 charges), heal (6 charges), lesser restoration (2 charges), mass cure wounds (5 charges), regenerate (7 charges), or warding bond (2 charges).

You can also use an action to cast one of the following spells from the staff without using any charges: animal friendship (snakes only), detect poison and disease, poison spray, or spare the dying.

Staff of the Python

This also functions as a staff of the python. This version of the staff's giant constrictor snake uses your spell save DC for its armor class and your spell attack bonus for its attack rolls, and it has a bonus to all saving throws equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. If the giant constrictor snake is reduced to 0 hit points while the is transformed, it immediately reverts to its form, and this property can't be used again until the next dawn. When you mentally command the snake, you can choose for it to use its action to cast any of the 's spells on its turn, requiring no components; doing so expends charges and uses your spell attack bonus and spellcasting ability modifier as normal.

Venomous Strike

When you hit a creature with this or when the transformed giant constrictor snake hits a creature with its bite, you can expend 1 of the 's charges to deal an extra 2d6 acid or poison damage (your choice). If either of these extra damage dice roll a 6, or if both dice roll a 1, the target must also succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or become poisoned until the end of your next turn, or the snake's next turn if it made the attack.

This silver badge of a four-fingered hand represents the story of the selfless medic, a patron saint of field doctors among humankind. Even if you're not attuned to the badge, you gain a +5 bonus to Wisdom (Medicine) checks you make while wearing it.

While attuned to the badge and wearing it, you gain the following benefits.

Reattach Limb

You can use an action to pin the badge to a detached limb and hold it to the body it was lost from, provided that they're both within your reach. When you do, the badge magically reconnects the limb and restores its typical function. The badge then loses this property as well as the other two properties described below.

Selfless Healing

You can use an action to touch a creature and spend one Hit Die. Roll the Hit Die: the touched creature then regains hit points equal to your Constitution modifier plus twice the number rolled. Once a creature regains hit points in this way, it can't do so again until it finishes a long rest.

Triage

You have proficiency in the Medicine skill. In addition, you can use a bonus action to look at a creature and make a DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check. On a success, you can determine if the creature has half its hit points or fewer remaining.

This leather bag has 3d6 glimmering red beads inside it when found. A bead feels pleasantly warm while held. You can use an action to withdraw a bead from the bag and place it in an unlit brazier (or similar vessel), causing a continual flame to sputter to life within the brazier and destroying the bead.

This three-inch-diameter ball of magical web is especially strong. Upon closer scrutiny, countless spiderlings skitter around inside it. You can use this ball of web as a material component when casting the web spell. After doing so, the ball unravels and disappears.

When you cast the spell in this way, its area becomes a 30-foot cube, and a giant spider appears in a space of your choice that's covered by the web. The spider is friendly to you and your allies and vanishes when the spell ends, taking its turns on initiative count 20. On its turn, the spider moves and attacks the nearest non-friendly creature within 30 feet of the web, using the webbing to its advantage as best it can.

You can use an action to string a nonmagical bow with this item to transform the bow into a magical one. When you hit a creature with a ranged attack using the bow, that creature suffers from a magical barb. A creature with a barb that willingly moves before the start of your next turn takes 3d4 piercing damage as the barb cuts into it; until the end of the turn, the creature's speed is reduced by a cumulative 5 feet for each 4 you roll on the dice.

A creature can only be affected by one barb at a time. A barb created in this way disappears at the start of each of your turns or when it deals damage to a creature that moves. Removing the bowstring from the bow makes the bow nonmagical once more.

This pair of swords counts as a single item for the purpose of attuning to them. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with these magic weapons; this bonus extends to any Strength check you make or Strength save DC used when you attempt to shove a creature.

While holding one of the swords, you can use an action to cause the other one to teleport to your empty hand or to the ground at your feet (your choice). When you do, the blade reappears in a plume of minuscule insects.

Hurl

When you take the Attack action while holding both swords, you can choose to forgo making any attacks to instead force a creature within 5 feet of you that's no more than one size larger than you to make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the blades come together to grab and throw the creature up to 20 feet away from you and knock it prone. If the thrown target strikes a solid surface, the target takes 1d10 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was thrown. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take half as much damage and be knocked prone.

Insect Plague

While holding both swords, you can use an action to cast the insect plague spell from them (save DC 15). This version of the spell ends at the start of your next turn, instead of its normal duration, and doesn't require you to concentrate on it. For the duration, one of the two swords disappears (you choose each time); the sword reappears in your hand or at your feet when the spell ends. This property can be used twice, and the swords regain all expended uses of it daily at dawn.

While wearing this belt, you gain a +1 bonus to Charisma (Persuasion) checks you make, provided you only tell the truth. If you speak a deliberate lie while wearing it, the belt magically bursts into flames, destroying itself and forcing you to make a DC 13 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, any nonmagical legwear you're wearing is harmlessly immolated and turns to ash, provided it's made of a flammable material.

This javelin radiates heat from within when thrown. When you make a ranged attack with this magic weapon and speak its command word, it becomes primed to detonate. If the target is a creature and the attack hits, the javelin immediately explodes; on a miss, the javelin instead lands at a random point beyond the target within 30 feet of it. If the attack misses, or if the target isn't a creature (such as if you threw it at a point or an object), the javelin instead explodes at its location at the start of your next turn. If a creature moves the javelin before then, it explodes early.

When the javelin explodes, each creature within 20 feet of it must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw; the original target of the attack makes the saving throw with disadvantage. A creature takes 3d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Once the command word has been used, it can't be used again for 1 minute. After that time, it shouldn't be used again until the next dawn: each time it's used again before then, the javelin has a 50 percent chance to destroy itself when it explodes.

You must bleed onto the dagger as part of attuning to it. When you hit a creature with this weapon, it takes an extra 1d4 necrotic damage from the attack. You then regain a number of hit points equal to the extra necrotic damage dealt; if you have more than half your hit points remaining, you instead gain temporary hit points equal to the extra necrotic damage. You don't gain hit points or temporary hit points in this way if the target is a construct, ooze, plant, or undead.

Affix Bayonet

While holding the dagger, you can use a bonus action to affix it to either a heavy crossbow, pistol, or musket you're also holding. It takes an action to remove the dagger again. While the dagger is affixed to another weapon in this way, you can make a melee attack with the dagger while holding the other weapon. In addition, your attacks with the other weapon deal an extra 1d4 necrotic damage to any creature you hit with it, as if the attack were made by the dagger.

Curse

This weapon is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, your hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to your level.

This wooden figurine of an old bloodhound radiates with an earnest desire to find things. You can use an action to speak the figurine's command word and then wrap it in or press it against an object or surface that has a smell. A spectral hound then appears and begins to move toward the nearest other target with that smell within 1 mile of you. The hound moves at a speed of 20 feet per round, and it continues to search for 10 minutes. At the end of the 10 minutes, roll a d6. On a 1, the hound gives up the search. On any other result, it continues to search for another 10 minutes, up to a maximum duration of 1 hour. You can end the effect early by speaking the figurine's command word again using an action.

This hound can't locate a target beyond running water at least 10 feet wide or any thickness of lead (even a thin sheet) if it blocks a direct path between you and the target. In such a case, the hound moves to the farthest point it can before reaching the water or lead and then paws at the obstacle. If the hound can't detect any target within 1 mile of you, it huffs disappointedly and then disappears.

Once the figurine has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Weight: 0.075 lb.

Bolts of inspiration typically come in cases of 5. When you make a ranged attack with one, you can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to the attack roll. Hit or miss, the bolt then becomes nonmagical. On a hit, another creature of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of the target gains a special d4. Once in the next minute when that creature makes an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, it can roll that d4 and add the number rolled to the result. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use this d4, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. A creature can only have one d4 in this way at a time.

Other types of magic ammunition of this kind exist, such as arrows of inspiration meant for a bow, though bolts are most common.

This magic musket uses a bolt-loading mechanism. It shoots a bullet propelled by lightning when fired, which emits instantaneous bright light out to a range of 20 feet along the bullet's path.

Attack rolls with this magic weapon are made with advantage if the target is made of metal or is wearing metal armor. In addition, the first target you hit on a turn with it takes an extra 1d6 lightning damage; if you had advantage on the attack roll, you can roll the lightning damage's die twice and use the higher result.

Lightning Strike

The rifle has 3 charges, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target with an attack roll using this weapon, you can expend 1 or more of its charges to increase the number rolled on the d20 by the same number of charges, up to a maximum of 20, as if you rolled that number on the die instead. Regardless of the result, the target of the attack and other creatures of your choice within 10 feet of it that you can see must then make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 2d6 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one; this lightning damage is increased by 1d6 for each additional charge you expend after the first. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

This bow is carved in the likeness of a large-billed pelican. While holding the bow, you can use an action to speak its command word and touch an arrow that's nocked in it to another object within your reach; the object is then magically tethered to the arrow. You can also make a single attack with the bow using that arrow as part of this action; a tethered object doesn't alter the arrow's flight. A translucent, illusory pelican appears to carry the tethered object in its bill for the duration of the arrow's flight.

The tethered object can weigh no more than 5 pounds and must be able to fit in the palm of your hand. It remains tethered for 1 minute or until the arrow hits a target, at which point the object is released and drops to the ground below. The GM determines what happens when the object drops in this way: delicate objects, such as a vial of acid, may shatter on impact, or a bag of ball bearings may scatter in the surrounding area. If you target a point on a solid surface with the arrow (such as a wall or ceiling), a creature can use its reaction to catch the tethered object before it drops to the ground, provided the creature is within reach of the targeted point or directly below it.

This brass bead bracelet looks like a coiled centipede. While wearing it, you can speak its command word using an action to cause it to transform into a giant centipede in an unoccupied space that you can see within 5 feet of you. The centipede remains for 1 hour, until you speak its command word again using an action, or until it's reduced to 0 hit points. The centipede transforms back into the bracelet when the effect ends. The centipede appears with all its hit points; the first time this property is used each day after dawn, the centipede appears with 2d10 temporary hit points. If the centipede transforms back into the bracelet due to being reduced to 0 hit points, roll a d20: on a 1, the bracelet is destroyed.

The giant centipede is an ally to you and your companions. In combat, it shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

While wearing these bracers, you deal an extra 1d6 psychic damage the first time you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon or an unarmed strike on each of your turns. The bracers have 3 charges for the following properties. They regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

Mind Splinter

Whenever you deal psychic damage with the bracers, you can expend 1 of their charges to increase that damage by an additional 1d6. When you do, the next attack roll or ability check made by that target before the end of its next turn is reduced by the same number rolled on the additional d6.

Quick Thinking

Whenever you make either an ability check or saving throw that uses Dexterity or Intelligence, you can use your reaction to expend 1 of the bracer's charges to use the other modifier for the roll.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
This pair of bracers is always warm to the touch. While wearing them, you have resistance to fire damage.

Scorching Giant

You can use a bonus action while wearing the bracers to tap your fists together and duplicate the effects of the enlarge/reduce spell (enlarge option only), targeting only yourself and without requiring concentration. This version of the spell also increases your body temperature and the ambient heat of any metal that you're touching: you deal an extra 1d8 fire damage with any attack you make using an unarmed strike or metal weapon, and any creature within 5 feet of you that touches you, hits you with an attack, or ends its turn there also takes 1d8 fire damage. This property can be used twice, and it regains all expended uses of it daily at dawn.

These bracers carry a portion of a sahuagin priest's lingering magic. You gain the following benefits while wearing them.

Spells

You can use an action to cast either the bestow curse or hold person spell from the bracers (save DC 15). Once a spell has been cast in this way, it can't be cast from the bracers again until the next dawn.

Trident Mastery

You have proficiency with tridents. When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a trident, you can reroll the die; you must use the new roll.

Webbed Hands

While submerged in water, you gain a swimming speed of 40 feet.

Curse

This item is cursed, and donning the bracers extends the curse to you. You remain cursed in this way until you're targeted by the remove curse spell or similar magic. While cursed in this way, your attack rolls against sahuagin and sharks are made with disadvantage.

Weight: 1 lb.

This small log looks like an ideal campfire starter. It weighs 1 pound and is roughly a foot long.

When you add this log to a fire, it releases a pair of loud cracks. When viewed from the side, the log's cracks can be read like a makeshift clock, allowing you to tell the time. The log cracks again at the start of every hour for the duration of the fire.

Furthermore, the log reveals a series of glowing embers along its bark as it becomes covered in char. The embers appear along a series of parallel, fiery lines that run the length of the log, functioning as a cylindrical sheet of music. While the log burns, it releases a soft tune, as if played from a gentle guitar, that follows the music shown on the log. The music on the log changes and adjusts to fit the local scenery and discussion.

Despite burning, the log is never consumed by a fire, and it remains cool even when plucked from an active flame. Using an action to dust the log off causes any char and soot to magically flake away, leaving the log clean once again.

Weight: 6 lb.

Damage: 1d12 piercing

Properties: R, S, H

This lance looks like a modified cannon with a wooden vamplate. A chain dangles from the pointed front of the lance to the cannonlike base. This weapon has the heavy property.

Once on each of your turns, you can replace one of your attacks with the lance to make a special ranged attack with it. When you do, you fire the front of the lance at a target that you can see within 20 feet of you. The blast emits a thunderous explosion audible out to a range of 300 feet. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 piercing damage (without adding your Strength modifier), or 6d6 piercing damage if the target is an object or structure. If you hit a creature and roll a 6 on any of the d6s, the target is also pushed up to 10 feet away from you. The chain then automatically pulls the point back to its base, where it magically reattaches. You can use a bonus action when this happens to pull yourself up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space directly between you and the target.

While wearing this red velvet cape, you have advantage on any ability check you make to convince someone that you're a noble (or of similar status).

In addition, when you use an action to make a Charisma (Persuasion) check, you can choose to lace your words with magic from the cape. When you do, the creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be affected by the suggestion spell for up to 10 minutes (no concentration required). The save DC for the spell is equal to the result of the Charisma (Persuasion) check, up to a maximum of 15. The spell ends early if you're no longer wearing the cape. This property of the cape can't be used again until the next dawn.

Weight: 2 lb.

Damage: 1d8 piercing

If you hit a creature that is missing any of its hit points using this magic weapon, its damage die becomes a d10 for the attack, and it deals necrotic damage instead of piercing. Furthermore, when you slay a Small or larger living creature with this weapon, you immediately gain 1d10 temporary hit points; you lose these hit points early if you're no longer holding the weapon.

This armillary sphere is about 6 inches in diameter and features a unique glyph of each plane of existence. When left unattended, the rings slowly revolve and spin on their own. Over the course of one minute, you can orient the various rings to all align at a singular glyph, at which point you can speak the name of a location on the associated plane of existence. The sphere then lifts up, spins wildly, and creates a portal to the named location on the chosen plane (as if by the gate spell, except it can appear on your current plane of existence).. The gate is 10 feet in diameter and hangs in the air, facing you. The sphere then drops to your feet or into your free hand (your choice).

The gate remains for 1 minute. The area in a 60-foot radius centered on the gate where it appears in the new location is then suffused with holy power, granting it the benefits of the hallow spell for the next 12 hours (Everlasting Rest or Peaceful Rest extra effect only; you choose the creature types affected by its first effect).

Once the item creates a gate in this way, it can't do so again until 24 hours have passed, or 12 hours if the chosen location was on the same plane of existence as you.

Weight: 3 lb.

Damage: 1d6 slashing

Properties: F, L

While this weapon is on your person, you can't become drunk from nonmagical alcohol. When you hit a creature with this weapon and roll the highest number on its damage die, that creature must also succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned until the start of your next turn, as the weapon's alcoholic magic overcomes it. If the creature fails the saving throw by 5 or more, it also falls prone.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
While wearing this belt, you can use an action to automatically escape from any nonmagical grapple or restraint. In addition, your fists are considered to be +1 clubs, allowing you to make unarmed strikes with them as if they were weapons you're wielding with the normal properties of a club; if your Strength score is 17 or higher, the damage die becomes a d6.

Piledrive

Once per turn when you knock a creature prone and are wielding no other weapons, you can make a single unarmed strike with your fist (no action required) against that creature. Your attack roll for this unarmed strike scores a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

Takedown Reversal

When a creature within 5 feet of you misses you with a melee attack, you can use a reaction to force that creature to make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature falls prone, provided it's no more than one size larger than you.

This amulet is made from a repurposed horse's rein. While wearing it, you are considered proficient in the Animal Handling skill whenever you make a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check to interact with a Large or larger beast.

While wearing the amulet, you can use an action to cast the find steed spell from it. When you do, roll a d8 to determine what creature is summoned by the spell, using the table below. If that creature has already been summoned since the last dawn, the spell fails, the action is wasted, and this property of the amulet can't be used again until the next dawn. Otherwise, the steed appears beneath you (using the creature's normal statistics), allowing you to mount it as part of casting the spell. This version of the spell has a duration of 1 hour, and when it ends, the steed immediately disappears. The spell ends early if you dismiss the steed, if it's reduced to 0 hit points, or if you dismount it.

d8Summoned Creature
1Axe beak
2Camel
3Elk
4Giant goat
5Giant lizard
6Giant toad
7Lion
8Riding horse
Curse

This amulet is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you unless you're a creature of chaotic alignment. Whenever the find steed spell fails to cast as a result of attempting to summon a creature that had already been summoned since the last dawn, that creature appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. The creature is hostile toward you and takes its turns on initiative count 20. The creature remains for 1 minute or until it's reduced to 0 hit points.

m: Wondrous item · Rare · needs attunement by a bard, cleric, or druid
h:
This choker clasps around your throat with a discreet hinge and then magically slithers as it resizes to fit. The choker has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing it, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast either healing word (1 charge) or mass healing word (2 charges), using your spellcasting ability modifier.

Whenever you cast healing word or mass healing word while wearing the choker, you you can choose to change the nature of the spell for one or more affected targets. When you do, a target affected by the changed spell must make a Constitution saving throw, using your spell save DC. On a failed save, a target takes poison damage equal to the number of hit points the spell would normally restore and is poisoned until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage and isn't poisoned. A creature that can't be poisoned can still be poisoned in this way unless it has an Intelligence of 3 or lower.

m: Wondrous item · Varies · needs attunement by a spellcaster
h:
This dark, translucent orb has a twisting swirl of red, green, and blue inside. Cradling the orb is a twisted cage of obsidian. The orb is about six inches in diameter and can be used as a spellcasting focus. If you know the chromatic orb spell or have it prepared, this item also functions as the material component for that spell.

The orb has a number of charges based on its rarity, as shown in the table below. It regains all expended charges daily at dawn. You can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast the chromatic orb spell from it, using your spell attack bonus. The level of the spell is equal to the number of charges you expend, and the maximum spell level depends on the orb's rarity.

This dark, floor-length cloak is fashioned to look especially imposing. While wearing it, you can use a bonus action to mentally cause your shadow to appear up to three times your normal size. The effect lasts for 1 minute, until you end the effect (no action required), or until you're in an area of darkness.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
This silvery cloak resembles a snowy owl. While wearing it, you have resistance to cold damage, and armor you're wearing doesn't impose disadvantage on your Dexterity (Stealth) checks if it normally would. In addition, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while in snow, and difficult terrain composed of ice or snow doesn't cost you extra movement.

Furthermore, your ranged attacks with a bow, crossbow, or thrown weapon are silent if you're hidden while wearing this cloak. As a result, missing with such an attack doesn't reveal your location.

Weight: 2 lb.

Damage: 1d4 bludgeoning

Properties: L

This hollow wooden club releases a plume of spores whenever it's swung. A target hit with the club takes an extra 1d4 poison damage from the attack. If the club is under the effects of the shillelagh spell, the target must also make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw if you roll a 4 on the poison damage: on a failed save, the target is poisoned until the end of your next turn.

Although all conch shells can sound like the ocean, this one lets you actually hear what it's saying. While touching a body of water of at least 250 gallons, you can use an action to hold the shell to your ear and ask the water a question that can be answered with either "yes" or "no". The water will answer the question to the best of its understanding, such as "has another creature stopped to drink from you today?" or "is there something buried in the sand beneath you?" The response may sound different based on what's in the water—for instance, a blessed well of water may sound priestly, and a poisoned one may sound sick.

Once used, this property of the shell shouldn't be used again until the next dawn. Each time it's used again before then, the shell has a 20% chance of cracking in half and becoming nonmagical.

This ring is made with covolt, an elemental blue metal that carries stormlike properties. If you take lightning damage while wearing the ring, you can use your reaction to halve that damage. When you do, each creature within 5 feet of you (excluding yourself) must immediately succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take lightning damage equal to the amount you reduced.

While wearing the ring, you can use an action to create an electrical field around you. The field remains for 1 minute, until you end the effect (no action required), or until you're no longer wearing the ring. A creature takes 1d8 lightning damage from the field if it ends its turn within 5 feet of you or if it hits you with a melee attack while within that range. Once you create the field, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Weight: 2 lb.

Up to ten scrolls can fit within this magic scroll case, which always weighs 2 pounds. While the scroll case is on your person, you can read from a scroll within the case as if you were holding it, allowing you to cast a spell from a spell scroll within the case without retrieving it (provided you can normally do so). Furthermore, you have advantage on any ability check you make to cast or copy a spell from a spell scroll.

Whenever you cast a spell from a scroll in the case, there's a chance that the scroll isn't destroyed after casting the spell. The chance depends on the level of the spell, as shown on the table below.

Spell LevelChance of Non-Destruction
Cantrip; 1st-2nd50 percent
3rd-4th25 percent
5th5 percent

m: Melee weapon · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
Weight: 1 lb.

Damage: 1d4 piercing

Properties: F, L, T

This parrying dagger imbues you with a heightened sense of awareness. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This bonus also extends to initiative rolls, Wisdom (Perception) checks, and Dexterity saving throws you make while the dagger is on your person. While holding the dagger, you gain a +2 bonus to AC if you are using no shield.

Staggering Flourish

The dagger has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. When a creature you can see hits you with an attack while you're holding the dagger, you can use your reaction to expend 1 of its charges to force that creature to reroll the attack roll; it must use the new result. Hit or miss, the attacker then takes a -2 penalty to AC until the end of your next turn if it's within 5 feet of you, as the dagger magically disrupts its defenses.

The interior of this brass lamp is covered in soot. While holding the lamp, you can use a bonus action to speak its first command word to ignite it, filling the glass with a small, fiery orb. While lit, it sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. You can use another bonus action to speak the command word again to extinguish it.

While holding the lamp, you can use an action to speak its second command word. When you do, the flame roars to a powerful brilliance. All other creatures within 20 feet of you that can see the light and aren't averting their eyes must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw; a creature that's in dim light or darkness or that has the Sunlight Sensitivity trait has disadvantage on the saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is blinded until the end of your next turn. In addition, any nonmagical flames within 40 feet of the lamp are extinguished when you speak this command word. Once this property of the lamp has been used, its light goes out, and neither of its command words can be used again until the next dawn.

m: Melee weapon · Rare · needs attunement by a warlock
h:
Weight: 1 lb.

Damage: 1d4 piercing

Properties: F, L, T

When you hit a creature with an attack using this dagger, it takes damage from the attack as if it were hit by a beam of an eldritch blast spell you cast, using the spell's damage die and other effects associated with the spell. If you're not holding the dagger at the start of your turn, you can choose to have it magically appear in an open hand (no action required); the dagger must be on the same plane of existence as you.

Blood for the Old Ones

While holding the dagger, you can use an action to plunge it into your chest. When you do, you take 10 force damage, which can't be reduced in any way, and you can choose up to four creatures that you can see within 30 feet of you. Each chosen creature must then make an Intelligence saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d10 psychic damage and is incapacitated until the end of its next turn. Damage from this property ignores temporary hit points (including yours). Once a creature has taken damage from this effect, it has advantage on the saving throw against it for 24 hours. If your hit points are reduced to 0 as a result of using this property, each affected creature makes the saving throw with disadvantage; you automatically suffer one death saving throw failure for each time you drop to 0 hit points in this way after the first, resetting daily at dawn.

This key has a jagged crystal ball shard embedded in its end. While the key itself doesn't unlock any doors, it has 3 charges for the following properties, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

Keyhole Clairvoyance

You can use an action to insert the key into a keyhole and speak its first command word, expending 1 of its charges. When you do, you become blind with regard to your own senses, but can see through the other side of the keyhole (if any) as if you were on the other side of the lock. This effect lasts until you remove or let go of the key (no action required), at which point your senses return to you.

Lock Scrying

You can use an action to tap the key to a lock and speak its second command word. When you do, a minuscule emblem of an eye appears on the lock where you tap it. If a creature uses its action to examine the lock, the creature can notice the eye with a successful DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check. The eye remains for 7 days, until it's dispelled, or until you use this property on a different lock. While the eye remains, the divination key magically vibrates whenever a key or lockpick is used on the lock. Furthermore, while the eye remains on the lock, you can use an action to touch the key to your forehead and expend 1 of its charges. When you do, you become blind and deaf with regard to your own senses, and you can see and hear as if you were in the lock's space, looking outward from the lock on the side that bears the eye. At the end of your next turn, this effect ends and your senses return to normal unless you expend an additional charge to extend the effect for another round.

This magic silver chain has 8 charges, which are represented by the same number of twists at its bottom; the twists hold the chain together into a necklace. The chain regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, the chain comes untwisted. Then, roll a d20. On a 1, the chain becomes nonmagical.

While wearing the twisted chain, you can expend 1 or more of its charges to use the following properties.

Spells

You can use an action to expend 1 of the chain's charges to cast either detect evil and good, detect magic, or detect poison and disease from the chain. Alternatively, you can expend 2 of its charges to cast either locate animals or plants or locate object from the chain, or 4 charges to cast locate creature. Regardless of the spell that's cast from the chain, its ends magically drift and point toward the located target or the nearest detected one. A spell cast from the chain ends early if you're no longer wearing it.

Swap

Whenever you're targeted by an attack or spell, you can use your reaction to expend 3 of the chain's charges to force another creature that you can see (other than the attacker or spellcaster) within 60 feet of you to make a DC 16 Charisma saving throw. A creature can choose to fail the saving throw. On a failed save, you and the target both teleport, swapping places, provided there's enough space. The triggering attack or spell then targets the swapped creature instead of you.

This scroll appears to be a spell scroll. An identify spell reveals its true nature.

On the scroll are the apparent mystical words to a random 3rd-level spell; choose or roll a d8 to decide between bestow curse (1), fear (2), fireball (3), hypnotic pattern (4), major image (5), sending (6), stinking cloud (7), or tongues (8). Regardless of the spell, the words inscribed on the scroll are faulty: a creature that attempts to transcribe the spell or cast it by reading the scroll must immediately succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be incapacitated. A creature that's incapacitated in this way has a speed of 0. The creature can repeat the saving throw after 10 minutes have passed and whenever it takes damage for the duration, ending the effect on a success.

Once the creature succeeds on the saving throw, the scroll turns to ash and is destroyed.

This pair of gravity-defying bangles hang effortlessly in the air around your wrists. While wearing them, you emit a field of strange gravity, which extends outward from you in a 10-foot radius. While in the field, you and creatures of your choice are always under the effects of the feather fall and jump spells; affected creatures also gain a +2 bonus to AC against ranged weapon attacks, as the gravity surrounding you alters the path of incoming projectiles.

The bangles have the following properties, which you can use while wearing them.

Spells

The bangles have 10 charges and regain 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. You can use an action to expend 1 or more of their charges to cast one of the following spells from them (save DC 17): flaming sphere (2 charges), floating disk (1 charge), levitate (2 charges), reverse gravity (5 charges).

Gravity Crush

As an action, you can force each creature within the bangles' field to make a DC 17 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d6 force damage and is knocked prone. If the bangles' flaming sphere is within the field's area, the sphere glows like a small star until the end of your next turn; for the duration, a creature's speed is also halved when it fails the saving throw against the sphere's fire damage.

Hovering

You have a flying speed of 30 feet and can hover. This form of flight doesn't allow you to move more than 10 feet off the ground. If you fall from a greater height and aren't incapacitated, your fall ends 10 feet above the ground, where you resume hovering, taking no falling damage.

Move Field

When you use one of the bangles' properties as an action, you can also move the bangles' field, centering it on a point that you can see within 30 feet of you; you can move the field either before or after using the action. Alternatively, you can move the field using a bonus action. The field returns to you at the start of your next turn.

This small ceramic charm resembles a water droplet with a face. It's roughly two inches tall and can fit comfortably inside a typical water goblet. Its weight is negligible.

The charm's face changes depending on the humidity, impending weather, or water quality it's surrounded by. For example, its face becomes sickly if placed in water that's non-potable (including water that's contaminated or poisoned) or gently pleased when placed in drinkable water. Similarly, its eyes turn skyward when rain is imminent (typically 15-30 minutes before it starts falling). Its expression takes 6 seconds to change.

This blue three-pointed hat features brass accents in the likeness of an eagle. While wearing it, the normal range of your ranged weapon attacks is increased by half (rounded down to the nearest 5 feet), up to a maximum increase of 30 feet.

In addition, you can use a bonus action while wearing the hat to speak its command word, briefly enhancing your vision. When you do, you have advantage on the next Wisdom (Perception) check you make before the end of your next turn, and you also have advantage on the next ranged weapon attack you make before then, even if it would normally be made with disadvantage as a result of attacking at long range. These benefits end early if you're no longer wearing the hat. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

m: Melee weapon · Very Rare · needs attunement by a warlock
h:
Weight: 4 lb.

Damage: 1d6 bludgeoning (1d8 two-handed)

Properties: V

This staff can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff. When you make a melee attack with it, it has a reach of 15 feet, as a magical tentacle lashes out from its end. If the target is a creature, it takes an extra 2d6 psychic damage on a hit. The tentacle disappears immediately after the attack."

While holding the staff, you can use an action to cast the black tentacles spell from it, using your spell save DC. Once you do, the spell can't be cast from it again until the next dawn.

Eldritch Tentacles

Whenever you roll initiative, an obviously illusory tentacle appears from the ground at a point that you can see within 30 feet of you. At the start of each of your turns in combat, roll a d6; on a 6, another tentacle appears on the ground at a point that you can see within range. On each of your turns, you can use a bonus action to move each tentacle to another point that you can see within 30 feet of you and make a melee spell attack against a creature within 10 feet of it, using your spell attack bonus; each tentacle must target a different creature. On a hit, a creature takes 1d6 psychic damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. A tentacle remains for 1 minute, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you're incapacitated or die. You can have up to three of these tentacles at a time.

This brass pipe features a warm, glowing vestibule at its end, and its brass fixtures are polished to a golden finish on the handle. You can use a bonus action while holding the torch to pull a short cord that hangs from the top of the pipe, just below the vestibule. Pulling the cord allows you to activate the torch's light, change the light's radius, or extinguish it. While lit, the torch sheds bright light in a 5- to 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional number of feet equal to the chosen radius. If you take lightning damage while the torch is on your person, the minimum and maximum radiuses of the torch's light are doubled for 1 hour.

This brass ring features a complex series of contained gears within its casing, allowing its outer shell to spin around an inner mechanism. The outer shell has six runes on it, one for each of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, and thunder. While wearing the ring, you can use a bonus action to enchant a weapon you're holding with one of the listed damage types of your choice. The enchantment lasts for 1 hour, until you remove the ring, or until you use this property of the ring again. While enchanted, the weapon deals an extra 1d6 damage of the selected damage type. Once a rune has been used to enchant a weapon in this way, that rune and its corresponding damage type can't be chosen again until the next dawn.
Any nonmagical markings written or drawn with this quill can be completely erased by brushing them away with its feather.

m: Wondrous item · Legendary · needs attunement by a creature missing an eye
h:
This metal sphere is the size of an eyeball with a glass iris. Its weight is negligible. Even if you aren't attuned to the sphere, it functions like a normal eye while it's in your eye socket; it doubles as a magic spyglass if you look through only the sphere.

If you're attuned to the sphere and have it in your socket, attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls, and creatures gain no benefit from half cover against your ranged attacks. You also gain the following two benefits:

Headshot

Whenever you score a critical hit on a ranged weapon attack, the target must also succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the start of your next turn.

Iron Focus

Whenever you make a ranged weapon attack as part of the Attack action on your turn and haven't moved during this turn, you can choose to reduce your speed to 0 until the start of your next turn and enhance the accuracy of the attack. Each time you use this property, the number you need to roll on the d20 to score a critical hit on a ranged attack roll against that target is reduced by 1, down to a minimum of 15. This benefit ends once you score a critical hit, attack a different target, or move.

Planar energy from the Feywild has imbued this cloak with latent trans-dimensional magic. While wearing it, you can magically sense the direction to any portal to the Feywild within 1 mile of you. The cloak has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn, or all expended charges if you are a fey, have the fey ancestry trait, or are in the Feywild. While wearing the cloak, you can expend 1 of its charges to cast the misty step spell. When you do, you can choose to cause flowers to grow from the ground and bloom in any space within 5 feet of where you leave or appear as part of the spell (your choice each time). When you do, other creatures within those spaces must then succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn or until you or your companions do anything harmful to it.

Weight: 2 lb.

Damage: 1d8 piercing

This war pick features a thrown punch as its hammer-ended side. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While holding this weapon, your unarmed strikes use a d8 damage die, unless it's already higher.

The weapon has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 of the weapon's charges to make an unarmed strike.

When you hit a creature with such an unarmed strike or with an attack using this weapon, you can expend 1 of its charges to force that creature to make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw; a creature is immune to this effect if it can't be charmed. On a failed save, the target is compelled to fight you for 1 minute. For the duration, the target has disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures other than you; if the target makes an attack roll with disadvantage in this way, you can use your reaction to make an unarmed strike against it, provided it's within your reach. The effect ends early if you attack any other creature or end your turn more than 30 feet away from the target.

m: Melee weapon · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
Weight: 2 lb.

Damage: 1d8 bludgeoning

The head of this flail is the clenched fist of a retired iron golem, which is connected by a chain to the rest of its hollowed gauntlet. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When you make an attack with this weapon, you can use your bonus action as part of the attack to first reel in the chained fist to the top of the flail. When you then make the attack, the fist rockets from the top of the weapon, increasing your reach with the weapon by 10 feet for that attack and scoring a critical hit with it on a roll of 18-20 on the d20. If you score a critical hit against a Huge or smaller creature in this way, the target must also succeed on DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

Reel Big Punch

You can use an action to reel in and overcharge the rocketing fist. When you do, the reeled-in fist flies out from the weapon in a 30-foot line that's 5 feet wide. Each creature within the line must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 5d8 bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails the saving throw by 5 or more is also knocked prone. The fist and chain are then reeled back in to the weapon's normal length. This property can be used three times, and the weapon regains all expended uses of it daily at dawn.

While wearing these rings on your matching thumb and forefinger, you can extend them to make a gesture of a pistol. Once per turn when you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with a special one using the rings by making this gesture, which has a range of 60 feet. Make a ranged spell attack with the rings, using a spell attack bonus of +5; if you're proficient with pistols, you can instead use your normal attack bonus as if you were wielding a pistol. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 + 3 force damage as a bullet of magical force rockets from your fingers to strike it. If you roll the same number on the damage dice, the target is also pushed up to 5 feet away from you.

You can replace multiple attacks in this way with multiple pairs of the rings (a maximum of twice per turn).

Weight: 2 lb.

Damage: 1d8 bludgeoning

Three jingling bells are attached to the handle of this flail, which uses 3d4 for its damage dice instead of 1d8. While holding it, you have advantage on Dexterity saving throws. In addition, whenever you roll a 1 or 20 on an attack roll made with this magic weapon, hostile creatures within 15 feet of you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be affected by the hideous laughter spell (no concentration required); this version of the spell ends at the end of your next turn.

Weight: 1 lb.

Damage: 1d4 piercing

Properties: F, L, T

Whenever you roll a 4 on this weapon's damage die, you can roll another d4 and add it to the total. You can continue to roll d4s in this way until you roll a number other than 4, up to a maximum of three additional times.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement by a wizard
h:
This stained leather tome is equal parts spellbook and cookbook. You gain a +5 bonus to any ability check you make using cook's utensils while attuned to it. When found, the book contains the following spells, which are wizard spells for you while you're attuned to it: create food and water, goodberry, grease, heroes' feast, and purify food and drink. It functions as a spellbook for you, and you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells. When you cast a spell and use this book as a focus for it, the air around you in a 5-foot radius is filled with the delicious scent of homemade cuisine (your choice each time).

The book also has 7 charges for the following properties. It regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the book dissolves into a delicious (but hot) soup.

Culinary Casting

While the book is on your person, you can expend 1 or more of its charges when you cast one of the spells listed above. For each charge you expend, the level of spell slot needed for that casting of the spell is reduced by 1. If you reduce a spell's slot level to 0 in this way, you can cast the spell from the book even if you don't have it prepared.

Magic Cake

While the book is on your person, you can use a bonus action to expend 3 of its charges to magically produce a small slice of cake. The cake appears on a small plate either in your hand or in the hand of a willing creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. You choose the flavor of the cake each time, as well as which of the following magical benefits it has. The cake grows stale and loses its magic after 1 hour. A creature holding the magic cake can use an action to eat it and gain the chosen benefit:

  • The effects of one poison or 1 level of exhaustion affecting the creature (your choice) are suppressed for 1d4 hours.
  • The creature regains 3d8 hit points.
  • The creature makes your choice of either Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution checks with advantage for the next 1 minute.
Temperature Control

When you cast a spell that deals either cold or fire damage, you can choose to change that damage type to the other. If you change fire damage to cold damage in this way, the spell no longer ignites flammable objects.

m: Wondrous item · Rare · needs attunement by a paladin
h:
This pair of golden gauntlets radiates with inspirational vigor. They have 3 charges and regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

Spells

While wearing the gauntlets, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 of their charges to cast either the heroism or shield of faith spell from them, using your spellcasting ability modifier. Alternatively, you can cast a spell in this way as part of using your Lay on Hands feature; the target of the spell must be the same one you touch. When you do, the spell doesn't require your concentration, but it ends early if you cast another spell again in this way.

Replenish Health Pool

While wearing the gauntlets, you can use an action to expend any number of their charges to replenish a number of hit points to your Lay on Hands pool equal to 5 times that number of charges spent, up to your maximum.

If you're holding a different weapon in either hand and are wearing these gloves, you can use your reaction when you miss with an attack roll using one of those weapons to reroll it. You must use the new result. If the new attack roll hits, it deals an extra 1d6 damage of the weapon's type.

Face Me!

When you roll initiative or as a bonus action on a following turn, you can choose to shout a challenge at a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. For the duration, the target must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw the first time it attempts to move away from you on each of its turns. On a failed save, it can't move away from you until the start of its next turn. This effect lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you attack any other creature, if you cast a spell that targets a hostile creature other than the target, or if you end your turn more than 30 feet away from the target. This property can be used twice, and it regains all expended uses of it daily at dawn.

These leather gloves feature small nodes of repurposed magical technology. While wearing the gloves, you gain a +5 bonus to any ability check you make using tinker's tools. In addition, you can use your Intelligence modifier in place of your Dexterity modifier whenever you make a Dexterity check with your hands (such as to pick a lock, tie a knot, or tinker with a gadget).

You gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks you make while wearing these magic gloves. They have 6 charges and regain 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the gloves, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 of their charges to use one of the following properties:

Burst of Agility

Your speed increases by 10 feet until the start of your next turn, and you have advantage on the next Dexterity check or Dexterity saving throw you make before then.

Swooping Escape

You become invisible until the start of your next turn or until you make an attack or cast a spell. For the duration, you also gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.

Treasure Sense

You magically sense what's inside a container you're touching, such as a chest or purse. You determine the general nature of what's inside (such as "a sword" or "a handful of coins"). The space inside the container can be no larger than 10 feet in any dimension.

Weight: 10 lb.

Damage: 1d12 piercing

Properties: AF, LD, 2H

This wide-mouthed golden firearm burns with a heat from within. It requires no ammunition, instead creating concentrated blasts of fire, but can still fire only once when you use an action, a bonus action, or a reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make. The weapon uses 2d8 for its damage dice, instead of 1d12, and deals fire damage instead of piercing. Hit or miss, any creature within 5 feet of the original target when you make a ranged attack with this weapon (including the target itself) must then succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d8 fire damage.

Overcharge

While holding the weapon, you can use an action to further concentrate the weapon's firepower. When you do, the weapon releases a gout of flame in a 60-foot line that's 5 feet wide, extending from you. Each creature within the line must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 6d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once this property of the weapon has been used, it shouldn't be used again until the next dawn. Each time it is used again before then, the weapon has a cumulative 25 percent chance of backfiring and causing an explosion (instead of this property's normal effects). When this happens, this property can't be used again for 1d4 + 1 days, and each creature within 5 feet of you must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw; you automatically fail the save. A creature takes 6d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

Weight: 5 lb.

A pack of golem clay weighs 5 pounds and is roughly the size of a large brick. You can spend 10 or more minutes molding the clay into a Tiny sculpture. Once you've done so, you can use an action to speak the clay's command word to animate it as a mindless golem, treating it as a Tiny object. The golem can perform simple tasks at your command. It has AC 13, 1 hit point, a Strength and Dexterity of 2, and it can't attack.

Once on each of your turns, you can verbally command the golem (no action required) to walk, swim, or climb—as appropriate for the golem's form—up to 15 feet and interact with an object. The golem remains animated for 1 hour, at which point it crumples into a lump of clay again. If it drops to 0 hit points, it immediately ceases to be animated, but it can be remolded and then animated once again. The golem and its clay are destroyed if it takes 10 or more damage in a single turn.

These magic bagpipes sound like honking geese. You can use an action to play three harsh notes in rapid succession to magically summon a swarm of geese in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you. Use the swarm of ravens statblock for the geese, except that its hit point maximum is doubled. The swarm takes its turn immediately after yours and attacks the nearest target that it can see. The swarm disappears after 1 minute or when it's reduced to 0 hit points. Once the bagpipes summon a swarm of geese in this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

If you're proficient with bagpipes, the geese are friendly to you and your companions unless you harm them. If you aren't proficient with bagpipes, the geese are hostile.

Weight: 6 lb.

Armour Class: 2

A creature must have a Strength score of 15 or higher in order to wield this heavy shield. It can also be used as an anvil for the purposes of smithing.

The shield has 3 charges, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the shield, you can use your reaction to speak its command phrase ("By the Forge!" in Dwarvish) and expend 1 of its charges when an attacker that you can see within 5 feet of you misses you with a melee attack. When you do, you cause a shower of scalding embers to erupt from the surface of the shield as the weapon grazes against it, dealing 1d8 fire damage to the attacker. A creature that takes this damage must also make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw if it made the attack with a metal weapon. On a failed save, the creature immediately drops the weapon; a creature takes 2d8 fire damage if it picks up the weapon before the end of the turn.

This 4-inch-tall bone sculpture weighs half a pound. You can use an action to place it on a gravesite or a corpse where it magically remains until a creature uses an action to remove it or until 10 days have passed, at which point it topples over. While the sculpture remains there, the creature is under the effects of the gentle repose spell, and the sculpture slowly bleeds from its eyes, which pools below it in a tiny well at its base. Regardless of how long the sculpture bleeds in this way, the blood never spills over from the well.

Once the sculpture is removed from the target or topples over, the pooled blood vanishes, and the sculpture can't be used again until 5 days have passed.

This pocketwatch-sized device opens to reveal a series of small holes. Along the bottom is a dial with labels for "Dwarvish," "Elvish," "Gnomish," and "Halfling." You can use a bonus action to change the dial. While the device is opened, any sentence spoken in the selected language within earshot of the device is automatically translated and spoken again through the device in Common. The repeated sentence sounds slightly tinny, and conveys the literal meaning of what's spoken.

This fragile ornament has a series of three numbered dials around its circumference. You can use an action to throw the ornament at a point that you can see within 30 feet of you, shattering and destroying the ornament. When you do, roll a d20 three times, recording each result. Alternatively, you can use an action before throwing the ornament to choose each result.

The ornament explodes into a flurry of festive décor that decorates the area in a 60-foot radius, centered on the point and spreading around corners. Use the result of the first d20 to determine the amount of décor (where 1 is a little, and 20 is a lot), and the second two results to determine the type or themes of the celebration. The decorations turn to glitter and then disappear after 7 days or when they're removed from the area in which they appeared.

3Astrological (you choose)

5Winter

13Wedding

15Mourning
