20Other (you choose)

Weight: 6 lb.

Damage: 1d10 slashing

Properties: H, R, 2H

This halberd features multiple blades that look like talons. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While attuned to the weapon, you can see normally at twice the normal distance in clear conditions, and you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

The halberd has 6 charges for the following properties. It regains all expended charges daily at dawn.

Flight

You can expend 1 of the weapon's charges as a bonus action to fly through the air to an unoccupied space that you can see within 20 feet of you. If you make an attack with the halberd immediately after landing in the new space, the attack roll is made with advantage.

Fling

When you hit a Large or smaller creature with the weapon, you can expend 1 of its charges to force the target to make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target is thrown up to 20 feet away from you and knocked prone, or 30 feet if you used the Flight property immediately before attacking the target. If a thrown target strikes an object, such as a wall or floor, the target takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was thrown. If the target is thrown at another creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take the same damage and be knocked prone.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
These wooden sandals have a split toe, ending in a cloven hoof. To attune to the sandals, you must be wearing them for the entire attunement period. Afterward, your feet and legs magically transform into those of a hooved fiend, absorbing the sandals into your body; you choose the color of your legs' skin when you attune to them. The sandals can't be removed as long as you're attuned to them.

While attuned to the sandals, you have resistance to fire damage. In addition, your Intelligence and Charisma scores increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Hellion's Stomp

The sandals have 4 charges and regain 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. While you're attuned to the sandals, you can use an action to expend 1 of their charges to stomp the ground beneath you and create a 30-foot line of smoldering earth and licking flames, originating from the ground at your feet. The line is 5 feet wide. Each creature within the line when it appears must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 6d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. The cracks cool immediately afterward, leaving behind scorchmarks and the smell of brimstone.

While wearing this hennin, you gain a +1 bonus to any Charisma check you make when interacting with fiends. In addition, you can use an action to cast the produce flame cantrip from it, using a spell attack bonus of +5. When you do, the spell ignores resistance to fire damage (but not immunity) if the target is a fiend, and the flame smells faintly of brimstone.

If you're a tiefling, the hennin's bonus to interact with fiends increases to +3. Furthermore, when you cast the produce flame cantrip from the hennin, it uses your level and spell attack bonus; the spellcasting ability is the same one used for other spells gained from your Infernal or Fiendish Legacy trait.

This tall knight's helm is made in the likeness of a chameleon. While wearing it, you can look in any direction without turning your head, unless it's directly behind you.

In addition, you can use an action to change the pattern and color of yourself and anything that you're wearing or holding. The change is illusory, and it ends as soon as you willingly move more than half your speed on a turn, when you choose to end the effect (no action required), or if you're no longer wearing the helm. If you change your appearance in this way to better blend into your surroundings, Wisdom (Perception) checks made to see you have disadvantage until you change your appearance again or your surroundings change.

You gain a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this helmet. In addition, you have advantage on any Intelligence or Wisdom check you make to determine where you are or to get your bearings, and you count as one size larger for the purpose of any effect that would allow you to push a creature or cause you to be pushed.

Raging Stampede

You must also be attuned to the axe of the minotaur in order to use this property. When you move at least 20 feet in a straight line and then immediately hit a creature with a melee attack, you can choose to force that creature to make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target is pushed up to 10 feet away from you and knocked prone; it must be no more than one size larger than you. If a creature made an opportunity attack against you as a result of this movement, you make the attack roll at the end of the line with advantage.

While wearing this silver helmet, you can't be moved against your will. Furthermore, once per turn when you make an unarmed strike, you can choose to make the attack with your head. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 force damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike, and is pushed up to 5 feet away from you. If you moved 20 or more feet straight toward the target immediately before making this attack, you have advantage on the attack roll, and on a hit, the target is pushed up to 10 feet instead.

If a pushed target strikes a solid surface or another creature that is larger than it, the target takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 5 feet it was pushed. If the target is pushed into another creature that is its size or smaller, that creature must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or take the same damage and be knocked prone.

Ring of the Ram

If you're also attuned to a ring of the ram, you gain a +1 bonus to AC while wearing the helmet, and the helm's Strength save DC is increased to 15.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement by a ranger
h:
This leather hood focuses your hunter's instincts. While wearing it, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks, and you have blindsight out to a range of 10 feet. Whenever you cast hunter's mark, a spectral falcon appears and flies around you until the spell ends. For the duration, whenever you hit a target marked by the spell with an attack, the falcon swoops down and strikes the target for an additional 1d6 force damage. The target must be within 120 feet of you.

The hood has 4 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the hood, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast the hunter's mark spell from it. This version of the spell doesn't require concentration, but the spell ends if the target drops to 0 hit points. You can mark multiple creatures simultaneously when you cast the spell in this way by expending additional charges: the number of creatures you can mark is equal to the number of charges you expend.

While wearing this magic bandolier, you can use your reaction when you roll initiative to make a single attack with a ranged weapon you're holding against a target within the weapon's normal range. If you're not already holding a ranged weapon, you can cause one to magically teleport to your open hand or hands as part of this reaction, provided the weapon is on your person.

The bandolier produces its own +2 firearm bullets, which can be loaded into a weapon as part of the bandolier's reaction when you roll initiative. These bullets are special, exploding immediately after the attack. Hit or miss, the target and each other creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 fire damage; the original target automatically fails this save if it was hit by the attack. If a special bullet that's removed from the bandolier isn't fired before the end of your next turn, it disappears in a small, crackling plume of smoke (like a firecracker). 1d4 missing special bullets reappear in the bandolier daily at dawn, up to maximum of 4.

Other types of magic bandoliers of this kind exist, such as ones that produce +2 bolts meant for crossbows, though ones that produce +2 firearm bullets are most common.

While wearing these knitted socks, you can use an action to wipe your shoes off (as if on an entry mat). When you do, your shoes, socks, and feet are magically cleaned, dried, and free of dirt or grime.

This slender, handleless walking cane has the insignia of a sword imprinted on the top. Regardless of a sword's shape or size, you can place it in the cane by sliding the blade into the insignia, as if the cane were a scabbard. When you do, the sword magically disappears into a special demiplane contained within the cane, and the top of the cane is magically transformed to represent the sword that was sheathed into the demiplane. If the sword has a crossguard, the cane can also create a handle that matches the guard. Only one sword can be stored within the demiplane at a time; you can withdraw a sword from it as though unsheathing it from the top of the cane.

Regardless of its form, the cane is indistinguishable from a normal cane, and neither it nor any sword stored within its demiplane can be targeted by divination magic, although a detect magic spell can determine that the cane itself is magical.

Weight: 3 lb.

Damage: 1d10 piercing

Properties: AF

This pistol has a mote of hellfire at the center of its 6-shot cylinder; it magically melts any nonmagical firearm bullet that's loaded in it, destroying the bullet. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it deals an extra 1d6 fire damage to any target it hits.

The pistol has 6 charges for the following properties. It regains 1 expended charge at the start of each of your turns and when you roll a 6 on any fire damage die you roll using the weapon. You can also use an action while holding the pistol to cause it to regain all of its expended charges; you do so by flipping out and spinning the weapon's cylinder, which emits a magma-like glow from within.

The weapon doesn't use ammunition and therefore lacks the loading property. Instead, each time you make a ranged attack with it, the weapon must expend 1 of its charges to magically create and fire a bullet made of brimstone.

Bedeviling Curse

When you hit a creature with a ranged attack using the pistol, you can expend 1 additional charge as part of the attack to force that creature to make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is cursed by a plume of devilish smoke that magically weakens it. While cursed in this way, the creature takes a cumulative -1 penalty to any attack roll it makes (to a maximum penalty of -3), and it has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against this weapon's named properties. This curse lasts for 1 minute, until you're incapacitated, or until you curse another creature with it.

Fan the Hammer and Flames

Once per turn when you take the Attack action with the pistol, you can forgo one of your attacks with it to expend 3 of the pistol's charges and release a 15-foot cone of damning flames from the holes in the barrel and cylinder. Each creature within the cone must succeed on a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d10 piercing damage and 4d6 fire damage.

This small magical rabbit's foot can easily fit in the palm of your hand. A jackalope's head, carved from an antler, is attached to one of its ends. When you roll a d20 while this item is on your person, you can choose to roll an additional d20 (no action required). You choose to do this after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. You then choose which of the d20s is used for the roll. If you use the second d20's result, the item's magic is then lost. Otherwise, this property of the item can't be used again until the next dawn.

Weight: 3 lb.

This metal wand weighs 3 pounds. The wand has 3 charges, and it regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can use an action while holding the wand to expend up to 3 of its charges. When you do, choose a number of metal bars that you can see within 60 feet of you, up to twice the number of charges you spent. The bars are then magically bent in whichever way you like (GM's discretion). The bars remain this way for as long as you concentrate on the effect (as if concentrating on a spell), to a maximum of 10 minutes, at which point the bars revert to their original shape. To be eligible, a metal bar must be nonmagical, can't be held or carried, and can be no more than 6 inches thick.

Weight: 2 lb.

Damage: 1d8 piercing

Properties: A, H, 2H

This bow is made from elements of a radiant horn and is strung with a fine braid of unicorn hair. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The weapon has 10 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. Whenever you make an attack with the bow, you can expend 1 of its charges to make the attack roll with advantage. If the attack hits, it deals an extra 1d10 radiant damage, and any friendly creatures within 5 feet of the target gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the number rolled on the d10. If you roll a 10 on the die, the radius of the effect increases to 30 feet.

Weight: 3 lb.

Damage: 1d6 slashing

Properties: F, L

This dark scimitar has inky swirls throughout its blade. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Once per turn when you would make a melee attack with it, you can choose to throw it at a creature that you can see within 15 feet of you instead (as if it had the thrown property). When you do, the blade's tentacle-like guard extends, but it remains gripped to your outstretched hand; hit or miss, the blade then retracts to your hand after the attack.

In addition, when you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this weapon, the target must also succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is covered by a spray of magical squid ink and is blinded for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns for the duration, ending the effect early on a success.

This crescent moon-shaped lantern has four commands. You can use an action to speak one of its command words if you're holding it.

The lantern's first command word causes it to shed bright light in a 10-foot radius between dawn and dusk, or a 20-foot radius between dusk and dawn. While lit in this way, it also sheds dim light for another 20 feet, regardless of the time. Speaking the command word again while the lantern is lit extinguishes it.

The lantern's second command word causes it to emit an instantaneous flash of bright light out to a range of 30 feet. When you do, any illusion within that bright light is dispelled if it was created by a spell of 3rd level or lower. This command word can't be used again until the next dusk.

The lantern's third command word causes any nonmagical light source within 30 feet of it to be extinguished. This command word can't be used again until the next dusk.

The lantern's fourth command word casts the moonbeam spell from it (save DC 15; 3rd-level version). This command word can't be used again until the next dusk.

Weight: 1 lb.

Damage: 1d4 piercing

Properties: F, L, T

This jade gardening knife is in the shape of a curled leaf. When you use it as part of making an Intelligence (Nature) or Wisdom (Survival) check, or an ability check using an herbalism kit, you can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to the total. Once you do, this property can't be used again until the next dawn. If you roll a 4 on the extra d4 in this way, the knife magically produces a single goodberry.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
While wearing this helmet, you gain a +1 bonus to AC, and you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened. In addition, at the start of each of your turns, if you lost any temporary hit points since the end of your last turn, you regain 1d10 of them (to a maximum of the amount lost); you must still have at least 1 temporary hit point to regain any in this way.

The helmet has 5 charges for the following properties. It regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. You must be wearing the helmet in order to use its various properties.

Frightening Roar

Once on each of your turns when you take the Attack action, you can expend 1 of the helmet's charges and forgo one of your attacks to release a thundering roar, which is audible out to 120 feet. Each hostile creature that can hear you within 10 feet of you must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw; this effect's range increases to 20 feet if you're in werelion form (see below). A creature has disadvantage on the saving throw if it's frightened. On a failed save, a creature takes 3d6 thunder damage and is frightened of you until the end of your next turn; a creature that fails the save by 5 or more is also knocked prone. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much thunder damage and isn't frightened.

Werelion Form

You can use a bonus action to expend 2 of the helmet's charges to physically change your form to resemble a werelion in hybrid form. You immediately gain 30 temporary hit points, which last for up to 1 hour or until you're no longer in this form. While in this form, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks, and you can make unarmed strikes with your teeth and claws, dealing piercing or slashing damage, respectively, instead of bludgeoning; these unarmed strikes use a d6 damage die, unless it's already higher. Your statistics are otherwise unchanged. You remain in this form until you have no temporary hit points remaining or until you end it early as a bonus action.

These cherry-shaped fruits are made of stone and are especially prized by xorn. They're most commonly found near veins of magical crystal. There are 1d4 + 1 fruits in a cluster when found. You can eat a fruit using an action to become temporarily made of stone; any equipment you're wearing or carrying also appears to be made of stone but otherwise functions as normal. For the duration, you have resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and while you remain perfectly still, you are indistinguishable from a statue of yourself. This effect lasts for 1 hour or until you take a total of 25 damage (after applying the resistance).

This small leather satchel was once used as a witch's component pouch for her spells. It can still be used as such, although it's also pierced by six magic needles that function as darts. A creature hit with a thrown dart takes an extra 1d6 poison damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 minute. When you hit a creature that you poisoned in this way with an attack, it takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. A poisoned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw against this effect is immune to it for the next 24 hours.

Hit or miss, a thrown dart turns to sulphuric ash after the attack, but it reappears piercing the pouch again at the next dawn.

This lute features a wooden face at its center. When played, it springs to life and sings alongside the music it makes, provided you know the words to the song. While the lute is singing in this way, you have advantage on Charisma (Performance) checks made with it.

The lute's voice is magically understandable to any creature that can understand at least one language, allowing you to communicate through song.

The voice is powerful and operatic. You choose whether the voice is masculine, feminine, or androgynous each time it sings. If you're a bard and are using the lute as a spellcasting focus, it can perform the verbal components of your bard spells for you (provided it can create sound), allowing you to cast such spells even while you're unable to speak.

m: Wondrous item · Uncommon · needs attunement by a spellcaster
h:
This tiny brass owl is about 5 inches tall and is virtually weightless. You can tap its head as a bonus action to cause its amber eyes to magically emit light, as if by a candle, or to extinguish them. If you place the owl on your shoulder (or similar), it remains there and magically steadies itself.

While attuned to the owl, you gain a +1 bonus to any ability check you make that uses your spellcasting ability.

The owl has a 1st-level spell slot, which you can use in place of your own when you cast a 1st-level spell while the owl is on your person (you must still concentrate on spells as normal). Alternatively, you can use an action to speak the owl's command word to expend that spell slot and duplicate the effects of the find familiar spell; the brass owl is the familiar, which magically animates itself, is a construct, and uses the owl stat block. This version of the stat block has resistance to all damage, immunity to poison and psychic damage as well as the poisoned condition, and 10 hit points. The owl ceases to be animated if it drops to 0 hit points or if you dismiss the familiar; reducing the owl familiar to 0 hit points doesn't destroy the item.

The owl regains its spell slot daily at dawn. If it's animated by the find familiar spell, the spell ends at the same time.

Weight: 2 lb.

Damage: 1d4 slashing

Properties: L

This sickle features magpie motifs, resembling its beak, coloration, and talons. Connected to the base of the sickle is a metal ball at the end of a chain, allowing it to be swung at a distance. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the finesse property. Once per turn when you take the Attack action and are holding no other weapons, you can make an extra melee attack with it as part of that action by using its ball and chain against a creature within 10 feet of you; you're proficient with the attack if you're proficient with sickles, and on a hit, it deals bludgeoning damage equal to 1d4 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier (treat the attack as if it were made with a flail).

Whenever you hit or miss a creature with an attack using the weapon's ball and chain, you can choose to force it to make a DC 15 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice). On a failed save, choose a weapon the creature's holding: that weapon becomes entangled in the sickle's chain. For the duration, you can't attack with the ball and chain, but attacks using the entangled weapon are made with disadvantage; neither you nor the other creature can move more than 10 feet away from each other without either you choosing to end the effect or the other creature choosing to drop the weapon. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

m: Wondrous item · Uncommon · needs attunement by a bard
h:
Whenever you expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration, you can force a creature within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC; the target has disadvantage on the save if it's a bovine creature (such as a cow or minotaur) and it automatically succeeds if it can't see you, if it already succeeded on the saving throw within the past 24 hours, or if it can't be charmed. On a failed save, the creature has disadvantage on any attack roll it makes against a target that isn't you until the end of its next turn. The effect ends early if you use this property again.

Matador's Pride

If you are also attuned to the matador's blade and are forced to make a saving throw against being frightened, you can choose to make a Charisma saving throw instead.

This necklace is made of swirling beads. If you become charmed, frightened, incapacitated (but not unconscious), or stunned while wearing this necklace, it breaks, and that condition immediately ends on you. The necklace ceases to be magical once it breaks, and the beads scatter in all directions.

This fountain of ink was made through alchemy using a mimic's blood, allowing its shapechanging magic to be influenced by writing.

When found, there are 1d6 + 4 uses of ink remaining in the fountain. You can spend 1 minute writing a detailed description of an object on a nonmagical piece of paper, expending a use of the ink; the paper then transforms into the object described. If the paper was in a book, the entire book transforms instead (provided it wasn't magical). Regardless of the written description, the object can be no larger than Tiny, and its weight, AC, hit point maximum, and other details are unchanged by the transformation; the object otherwise functions as it should. Describing a magical object does not impart those effects on the transformed object, nor can a transformed object be used as a material component for a spell. If you don't know the exact appearance or shape of an object you describe, the ink does its best to make reasonable assumptions. For example, if you describe a set of keys for the local treasury, the ink will create a set of keys that look appropriate, but wouldn't actually open it (unless you're exceptionally lucky).

Physical interaction with the object can immediately reveal it to be forgery, because its weight is likely different. A creature that uses its action to examine the object can determine that it is a forgery with a successful DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check. The transformation lasts for 24 hours or until the object is destroyed, at which point the object reverts to its original form, albeit tattered and damaged.

m: Shield · Rare · needs attunement by a spellcaster
h:
Weight: 6 lb.

Armour Class: 2

This magic shield glows softly under moonlight. While you're attuned to it, you know the moonbeam spell, which doesn't count against the number of spells you know or have prepared. It has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk.

While holding the shield, you can expend 1 of its charges as a reaction when you're hit with a melee attack. When you do, the shield releases a flash of brilliant moonlight. If the attacker can see the shield, the triggering attack roll takes a- 1d4 penalty, potentially causing it to miss. Hit or miss, each creature that can see the shield within 5 feet of you (other than you) must then make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw; a shapechanger makes this save with disadvantage. A creature takes 2d8 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The radiant damage increases to 2d12 if it's between dusk and dawn.

Weight: 10 lb.

Damage: 3d6 piercing

Properties: AF, LD, 2H

This wide-mouthed musket releases an audible and maniacal laugh whenever it's fired, in addition to the sound of the blast. This weapon uses 3d6 for its damage dice, instead of 1d12. When at least one of the weapon's damage dice rolls a 6, the target takes an additional 1d6 psychic damage from the attack. When this happens, if the target is a creature and can understand at least one language, it must also make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw; the target automatically succeeds on this save if it has immunity to psychic damage or can't be charmed. On a failed save, the next attack roll or ability check that creature makes before the end of its next turn is made with disadvantage.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
These dark boots are made with leather from a nightmare. While wearing them, you have resistance to fire damage, and you can cause harmless embers to spark from your heels when you walk (no action required).

Dread Aura

You can use a bonus action while wearing the boots to begin emitting an aura of dread with a 30-foot radius. Hostile creatures within the aura that can see you have disadvantage on saving throws against being frightened, and you can use a bonus action on each of your subsequent turns for the duration to force any hostile creatures within 10 feet of you make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you until the start of your next turn. This aura lasts for 1 minute or until you're incapacitated. For the duration, your steps sound like hellish chains being dragged across the floor. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Hellfire Steed

You can use an action while wearing the boots to summon a nightmare in your space, immediately becoming mounted on it (provided it is at least one size larger than you); this effect fails if there isn't enough space for it to appear. The nightmare is equipped with a saddle, bit, and bridle, which vanish when it disappears. The creature is bound to you for as long you remain mounted on it, and it is friendly to you and your companions. The nightmare disappears if it's reduced to 0 hit points or if you end your turn without being mounted on it. This nightmare can't use its Ethereal Stride action. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

You can spend 1 minute applying this oil to a full suit of plate armor. When you do, the armor animates and is under your control, using the statistics for an animated armor. The armor follows your verbal instructions to the best of its ability (no action required by you); you decide what action it will take and where it will move during its next turn, or you can issue a general command, such as to guard a particular chamber or corridor. If you issue no commands, the armor only defends itself against hostile creatures. Once given an order, the armor continues to follow it until its task is complete. The armor remains under your control until it's reduced to 0 hit points or until it falls unconscious due to a dispel magic spell, at which point it is no longer animated.

This flask of oil contains a swirling plume of ink. You can lather the oil over a patch of skin on a willing creature over the course of 1 minute. At the end of the minute, the oil magically creates a tattoo on the skin. You choose the tattoo's design. The tattoo remains indefinitely or until it's targeted by a dispel magic spell or similar magic. The flask has enough oil for 5 applications: a small tattoo consumes 1 application, a medium tattoo consumes 2, and a large tattoo consumes 3.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
This bone ocarina is carved in the shape of a skull and has playable holes that correspond to different body parts. The sound it makes is soft but haunting. You can use an action to play the ocarina to cast the blindness/deafness spell from it (save DC 16), covering the relevant holes on the skull for the effect you create. The target automatically succeeds on the save if it can't hear the ocarina. This version of the spell allows you to choose from the following additional options if the target fails its save, instead of causing it to be blinded or deafened: the target is muted for the duration or its concentration is broken. A creature muted in this way can't speak or perform the verbal components of spells.

Perishing Song

You can use an action to play this ocarina while covering all of its holes. When you do, each creature within 30 feet of you that can hear the ocarina (including yourself) must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is cursed by the ocarina for 1 minute. For the duration, each cursed creature must make the saving throw again at the end of each of your subsequent turns. A creature that fails this saving throw for a second time after the initial failed save falls unconscious with 0 hit points and is stable. A creature is no longer cursed in this way once it succeeds on the saving throw for a second time. Once this property is used, it can't be used again, and the ocarina loses this property once the curse ends on the last creature.

Weight: 18 lb.

Damage: 1d10 piercing

Properties: H, R, 2H

This black metal pike resembles a post of a particularly elaborate fence. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Summon Palisade

The pike has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. As a bonus action while holding the pike, you can expend 1 of its charges to create an iron fence of matching, duplicate pikes in a contiguous line on the ground that's up to 60 feet long, starting a point within 10 feet of you. The fence is 10 feet tall, 1 inch thick, perfectly vertical, and immovable for the duration. There is a 2-inch gap between each pike in the fence. Each 10-foot length of fence has AC 15, 15 hit points, and a damage threshold of 10. The fence has immunity to piercing, poison, and psychic damage and resistance to all other damage. The fence doesn't obscure the area, but it does prevent melee attacks from being made through it unless they are made with a piercing weapon. The fence remains for 1 minute, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you use this property again.

A creature that attempts to climb over the fence must make a DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. On a failure, the creature takes 1d10 + 1 piercing damage and fall prone on its original side of the fence.

While holding the pike, you can replace any of your attacks as part of the Attack action with a special one using one of the fence's posts. Treat the attack as if you were making it with the pike in a space adjacent to the fence. The post then swings out from the fence to attack before returning to its position the line.

This leather bound book magically records what happens to it as well as the creature carrying it. It describes even mundane happenings with flavorful language and narration. To even a dedicated reader, it seems like the book frames itself as the protagonist in its own story. The book creates its own illustrations, complete with dynamic paper pop-ups, based on the events surrounding it. While the book isn't sentient, it nevertheless writes with more energy and intrigue when visiting or exposed to new things. The book's pages return to blank daily at dawn, but are filled again within 24 hours.

You can use an action to hold the book aloft and describe, dramatically and aloud, how the book magically casts one of the following spells (save DC 16): comprehend languages, dimension door, hallucinatory terrain (the spell ends early if cast again), illusory script, major image, phantasmal force, or tongues. The book maintains concentration on the spells it casts; casting a second spell from the book that requires concentration causes the previous one to end. Once the book has been used to cast a spell, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

Weight: 1 lb.

This 4-inch-diameter stone disk weighs 1 pound and has a miniature hearth at its center. You can use an action to place the disk on an inanimate flat surface, at which point the hearth sparks to a low ember. The disk remains on the surface until it's removed using another action. While on the surface, you can rotate a stone dial around the disk's circumference. Rotating the dial all the way clockwise increases the temperature of the surrounding area by 50 degrees Fahrenheit, up to a maximum temperature of 80 degrees Fahrenheit; rotating it less than that increases the temperature by a proportional amount less. The fire in the disk's hearth burns more or less brightly depending on how much the temperature is increased in this way. The heated area extends outward from the disk up to 30 feet but is blocked by obstacles such as walls or ceilings.

Changes to an area's temperature take place over the course of 1 minute. Once the disk is removed from its surface, the area returns to its normal temperature.

This pair of brass knuckles is embedded with small, icy gemstones, which spark with blue light. While wielding the knuckles, you can use an action to speak their command word to cause one of the pair to disappear (your choice each time). When this happens, an ice-cold stein magically appears attached to the remaining knuckles, treating them as a makeshift handle. The stein remains until you use an action to speak the command word again or until you make an unarmed strike with your fist. When the stein disappears, the other brass knuckle reappears on your other hand, and the stein (with any drink inside) disappears into a special demiplane, where it remains until you speak the command word again. The stein is always comfortably cool and chilled to the touch, keeping any drink inside of it at a similar temperature.

Your unarmed strikes while using the brass knuckles use a d4 damage die, unless it's already higher. The first time that you hit a target with an unarmed strike using the brass knuckles on each of your turns, that target also takes an extra 1d4 cold damage from the attack. If your attack rolls would normally be made with disadvantage as a result of drinking too much alcohol, they're made as normal while using the brass knuckles.

Weight: 6 lb.

Armour Class: 2

This colorful buckler has a stained glass butterfly emblazoned at its center. While holding it, you have a +1 bonus to AC. This bonus is in addition to the shield's normal bonus to AC.

This shield pulls potential outcomes from other parallel timelines. It has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. When a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you is hit with an attack, you can use your reaction to expend up to 4 of the shield's charges. When you do, that creature gains a bonus to its AC equal to twice the number of charges you expend, potentially causing the triggering attack to miss, as echoes from other timelines successfully block the attack. This bonus to AC lasts until the end of the turn. Immediately after using the reaction, roll a d4: if the result is equal to or less than the number of charges you spent as part of the reaction, you take 1d4 psychic damage for each spent charge. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

Any text written with this quill is illegible to any creature other than a chicken. A chicken that reads the text can understand simple concepts or instructions, although it's under no obligation to follow them.

This hat features a single gold piece as a bolo tie for its whiplike hatband. While wearing it, you gain a +1 bonus to any saving throw you make against a trap. You also gain a +1 bonus to any ability check you make to discover or recover a piece of treasure you know about, such as picking the lock to a treasury or inquiring about a magical item's whereabouts.

In addition, when you fail a saving throw against a trap while wearing the hat, you can use your reaction to reroll the saving throw. You must use the new result. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

While wearing these rose-tinted glasses, whenever you make an ability check or saving throw against an effect that you failed the same check or save against on your previous turn for the first time, you gain a +2 bonus to the roll.

In addition, the glasses have a dial around their left lens, which is divided into 24 segments. Each segment represents 1 hour. You can use an action to rotate the dial counterclockwise by 1 or more hours. When you do, you can see the area around you as it appeared that number of hours ago through the glasses. Creatures that appear in the past in this way are blurred and indistinguishable.

You can use another action to rotate the dial clockwise, advancing it forward in time by 1 or more hours (to a maximum of returning it to the present). The dial returns to the present automatically 1 hour after it's turned.

The dial can be turned twice to a time other than the present, after which it shouldn't be turned in such a way again until the next dawn. Each time it's turned to a time other than the present again before then, there's a 25 percent chance that the glasses crack and become nonmagical.

You can use an action to tie this ribbon in a knot and speak its command phrase (a Gnomish tongue-twister) while focusing on another creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature must then succeed on a DC 13 Intelligence saving throw or be unable to speak or perform the verbal components of spells for 1 minute. The creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns for the duration, ending the effect on a success. The effect ends early if you or another creature unties the knot; it unties itself when the effect ends. A creature that can't understand at least one language is immune to this effect.

This ring has a second one outside of it which can be spun around idly. The spinning ring features interlocked and wringing hands. While wearing the ring, you can choose to automatically create a relevant, magical illusion around your hand whenever you make a recognizable hand gesture, such as tipping a hat (creating a fanciful hat atop your head), drinking from a cup (creating a steaming cup of tea), or stroking a beard (creating one for you while clean-shaven). The illusions created are Tiny and obviously magical, and they only serve to complete the illusion of the hand gesture.

While wearing this ring, you have a swimming speed of 30 feet and can breathe underwater. In addition, sharks are indifferent toward you and will not attack you unless you threaten or harm them.

The ring has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the ring, you can expend 1 of its charges using an action to point at a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. That creature must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d10 piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one, as it's attacked from below by a Large, illusory shark. The saving throw is made with disadvantage if the creature has fewer than half its maximum hit points remaining, and the damage increases by 1d10 each time that creature is targeted by this effect within 1 hour.

This ring slips on your finger, but can't be removed without also drawing blood. As a bonus action while wearing the ring, you can speak its command word to cause it to bite down and deal 1d4 necrotic damage to you, which can't be reduced in any way. For the next minute, the first time you hit a creature with a melee attack each turn, that creature takes an extra 1d4 necrotic damage. Whenever you deal necrotic damage in this way, you also gain the same amount of temporary hit points. When this effect ends, any remaining temporary hit points you have from it are lost. This property of the ring can't be used again until the next dawn.

Curse

This ring is cursed, and using the ring's property extends that curse to you. You remain cursed in this way until you're targeted by the remove curse spell or similar magic. While cursed, you gain the following flaw: "I have an urge to taste blood—even if it's just a little bit—every day. I mustn't let others find out."

m: Wondrous item · Uncommon · needs attunement by a druid or ranger
h:
This robe feels like a large, soft leaf. Even if you aren't attuned to the robe, any evidence of your travel while wearing it (such as footprints or disturbed underbrush) is magically hidden wherever you walk. As a result, other creatures take a -5 penalty to any check made to track you.

If you're attuned to the robe and are wearing it, the robe's magic extends to hide your group's travel while traveling together. In addition, you can use a bonus action to cast the barkskin spell on yourself from the cloak. Once you cast the spell, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

This rod resembles a collapsed tentpole with an embossed banner wrapped around it. While holding it, you can use an action to speak its first command word to cause the rod to elongate and plant itself in the ground at your feet, standing upright as a tentpole. The pole is 10 feet tall and is planted at a point on the ground within 5 feet of you. When this happens, the pole recreates the effects of the alarm spell, which covers a 30-foot-radius area centered on it; you designate whether the alarm is mental or audible, as well as what creatures won't set off the alarm.

While touching the tentpole, you can speak the rod's second command word using an action to cause a magical tent to unfurl from its top that's 40 feet in diameter. The tent creates a series of expedition-ready stations inside it: a cartography station, cooking station, medical station, and navigation station. When this happens, you can designate yourself or another creature within 30 feet of you to be a master of each station; each station must have a different master. The tent is always a comfortable temperature inside.

Cartography Station

A set of cartographer's tools appears at this station. The master of the station can use these tools to magically create a map of the area in a 2-mile radius with 1 hour of uninterrupted work (which can be done over the course of a short rest), provided the master is within the station. The tools move on their own in the master's hands while within the station.

Cooking Station

A set of cooking utensils appears at this station, as well as a lit fire pit; the fire is harmless, produces no smoke, and consumes no oxygen. The master of the station can use these tools to create a magical meal with 1 hour of uninterrupted work (which can be done over the course of a short rest), provided the master is within the station. Up to ten creatures can partake of the meal, and it provides enough nourishment to sustain each creature for one day.

Medical Station

A healer's kit appears at this station. The master of the station can expend one of its uses to restore 1d10 + 5 hit points to a creature within its reach with 1 hour of uninterrupted work (which can be done over the course of a short rest), provided the master is within the station. The master can also choose to end one of the following conditions on such a creature: blinded, deafened, or poisoned. Once a creature regains hit points in this way, it can't do so again until it finishes a long rest.

Navigation Station

A set of navigator's tools appears at this station. The master of the station can use these tools to magically tell which way is north and what the weather will be in the tent's current location for the next 24 hours. While within the station, the master can use an action to close their eyes and magically gain a bird's eye view of their current location, up to 100 feet in the air. While viewing their location in this way, they are deaf and blind with regard to their own senses. The master's senses return to normal at the start of their next turn, unless they use an action to continue using the bird's eye view.

A master of a station has advantage on any ability check it makes using a tool associated with its station while it's within 5 miles of the tent. The equipment disappears and these benefits end when the tent is collapsed into the rod. The equipment magically returns to its associated station if a creature other than the master holds it.

A creature touching the tentpole can use an action to speak the rod's third command word to collapse the pole (and any tent) into the normal rod. Once the rod is used to create a tent, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

These red bracers ripple faintly with a bloody shimmer. While wearing them, you can expend 2 Hit Dice to cast the vampiric touch spell from them (spell attack bonus +7) by forgoing making an attack as part of the Attack action. For the duration, you can forgo making an attack as part of the Attack action to make subsequent spell attacks with it. You can still only make one attack with the spell on each of your turns.

Curse

These bracers are cursed, and becoming attuned to them extends the curse to you. While cursed, you gain the following flaw: "The feeling of siphoning life with necromancy is euphoric—so much so that I feel compelled to do it every day. I mustn't let others find out."

While you're wearing this scabbard and have a weapon sheathed in it, you gain a +1 bonus to any Intelligence (Religion) check you make if you aren't holding any weapons. Furthermore, you can use a bonus action to stow a weapon created by a spiritual weapon spell you cast, sheathing it in the scabbard (even if another weapon is already sheathed in it). The weapon must be within 5 feet of you to stow it.

When you stow the spiritual weapon, the spell's duration is paused until you withdraw it from the sheath again (no action required), until you're no longer wearing the scabbard, or until you're incapacitated; a single casting of spiritual weapon can't be paused in this way for more than 24 cumulative hours. If the spell would normally require you to concentrate on it, it doesn't for as long as the weapon remains sheathed. While the spell is paused in this way, the scabbard emits a soft glow from its end. Withdrawing the spiritual weapon from the sheath causes it to reappear in a space within 5 feet of you.

This thick monastic scapular is dense and weighty, like a heavy leather apron. While wearing it, you have a base AC of 14 + your Dexterity modifier (to a maximum of +2). You can't benefit from wearing other armor while using this AC.

Earthen Slam

While wearing the scapular, you can use an action to stomp the ground beneath you, sending out a shockwave that affects all other creatures within 15 feet of you. Each creature must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage and 3d6 thunder damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked prone. This property of the scapular can't be used again until the next dawn.

Shield Battery

While wearing the scapular, you can use a bonus action to magically enhance its protection. You gain a +5 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn or until you remove the scapular. For the duration, whenever a creature hits you with a melee attack, that creature takes 5 bludgeoning damage. This property of the scapular can't be used again until the next dawn.

Weight: 3 lb.

Damage: 1d6 slashing

Properties: F, L

This magic weapon deals an extra 1d6 fire damage to any target it hits. While holding it, you can use a bonus action to speak its command word to cast the flame blade spell from it. This version of the spell uses the same attack bonus and ability modifier you use for the scimitar of flames; the spell ends early if you're no longer holding the scimitar. While holding only the scimitar and the blade created by the flame blade spell, you can attack with the flame blade using a bonus action after taking the Attack action with the scimitar.

This magic scimitar deals an extra 1d6 poison damage to any creature it hits. While attuned to it, you have resistance to poison damage and have advantage on saving throws against poison.

Incinerating Serpent

While holding the scimitar, you can use an action to speak its command word and create an instantaneous naga of pure light. Choose a space that you can see within 30 feet of you for the naga to begin in: it then instantly streaks forward from that space in a contiguous path, which is composed of up to ten 5-foot cubes. Each cube can be placed anywhere—vertically or horizontally—as long as it's adjacent to the previous one. Each creature within the naga's path must then make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 8d6 radiant damage and is poisoned for 1 minute; while poisoned in this way, the creature is also blinded. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much radiant damage and isn't poisoned. A creature poisoned in this way can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Naga's Restoration

If you die while the scimitar is within 60 feet of you, you are immediately restored to life with half your maximum number of hit points and are cured of any conditions affecting you. The scimitar then loses this property as well as its Incinerating Serpent property.

Weight: 3 lb.

Damage: 1d6 slashing

Properties: F, L

You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While you have more than half your hit points, you also deal an extra 1d6 slashing damage to any target you hit with it. In addition, whenever you deal damage to a creature using this weapon, you can move normally through its space until the end of the turn, which isn't considered difficult terrain for you. If you move through a creature's space in this way, you don't provoke opportunity attacks from it as a result of your movement until the end of the turn; if you end your turn in another creature's space in this way, you're magically returned to the nearest unoccupied space you moved through before entering that space.

You can read this scroll over the course of one minute. At the end of the minute, you name a creature within 5 feet of you, followed by a skill or tool with which you have proficiency. The named creature then also becomes proficient in the named skill or tool, and its name and new proficiency become inscribed on the scroll in beautiful calligraphy. The scroll then becomes nonmagical.

A scroll of superior mastery, a very rare version of the scroll, grants the named creature expertise with a skill or tool in this way: such a creature adds double its proficiency bonus whenever it makes an ability check using that skill or tool.

Weight: 20 lb.

This copper coin is embossed with rats walking around its edge. On either side is a matching radial pattern. You can use an action to speak the coin's command word and toss it onto the ground in a 5-foot-square space that you can see within 20 feet of you. When it lands, a 3-foot diameter tunnel appears in the middle of the space and extends downward up to 20 feet, complete with an affixed ladder. The tunnel ends early if it reaches an open area, and the ladder descends down up to 10 feet into the new area. The tunnel does not compromise any structural integrity when it appears.

The coin also expands, growing to fit the size of the tunnel's entrance; the coin then becomes the cover for the tunnel and weighs 20 pounds. The tunnel remains for 1 hour or until you use an action to speak the coin's command word again within 30 feet of it. The cover opens only at your command, which you can speak as a bonus action, although anyone can close it again. It is immune to the knock spell and similar magic, such as that of a chime of opening, but a creature can forcibly open it by succeeding on a DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check using an action. The cover closes itself after 1 minute if left open. A creature that's in the tunnel when it disappears is safely ejected from the top of it.

If the space where the tunnel appears is occupied by a Medium or smaller creature, that creature must also make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature falls down into the tunnel. On a successful save, the creature remains in the space but doesn't fall in.

When the tunnel disappears, the cover returns to its coin form. If the tunnel reached an open area below it, the coin falls into that area before the tunnel disappears at the end of duration; otherwise, the coin remains on the surface on which it landed. Speaking the command word to end the effect early allows you to choose whether the coin drops into the tunnel or remains on the surface.

Once the coin creates a tunnel in this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

When thrown, this dark throwing star is trailed by wisps of black smoke. This weapon has the light property, and you can engage in two-weapon fighting with it as if it were a melee weapon. If you're a monk, it's considered to be a monk weapon for you. When you hit a creature with this weapon, any nonmagical flames or lights within 10 feet of it are extinguished. This weapon deals an extra 1d8 force damage to any creature it hits, or 1d12 if the creature is in dim light or darkness. Hit or miss, the shuriken magically returns to your hand after making an attack with it.

Shadow Jump

This weapon has 4 charges, and it regains all expended charges daily at dusk. When you hit a target with this weapon, you can choose to expend 1 of its charges to teleport to an unoccupied space that you can see within 5 feet of it. If the new space is in dim light or darkness, you become invisible until the start of your next turn; the effect ends early if you make an attack or force a creature to make a saving throw.

m: Melee weapon · Rare · needs attunement by a bard
h:
Weight: 2 lb.

Damage: 1d8 piercing

Properties: F

You're proficient with this magic weapon while you're attuned to it, and you deal an extra 1d4 psychic damage to any creature you hit with it. If the creature has been been targeted by the vicious mockery spell since the start of your last turn, the psychic damage is increased to 1d6. In addition, while holding the weapon, your spell save DC for any vicious mockery spell you cast is increased by 1, and you can cast the spell as a reaction when a creature that you can see misses you with a melee attack or provokes an opportunity attack from you (rather than making the attack), targeting that creature with the spell.

Sheets of concentration typically come in small collections of 1d4 + 1 sheets. The sheets are blank when found. You can transform a sheet into a special spell scroll by expending a spell slot to cast a spell of 4th level or lower while touching the sheet; the spell must require you to concentrate on it. When you do, the spell has no effect, other than to transform the sheet, which slowly begins to fill with magical runes and writing. After 1 hour or at the end of the spell's duration (whichever comes first), the sheet is successfully transformed into the spell scroll. The sheet is wasted and becomes nonmagical if your concentration is broken before the end of that time or if you cease touching it.

This spell scroll is special: only you can cast the spell on it, and when you do, it doesn't require your concentration. A spell cast in this way ends early if you cast another spell in this way or if it remains in effect for 1 hour. If you're a wizard, you can use this spell scroll without having to read it, provided it's inside your spellbook and the book is on your person.

m: Melee weapon · Very Rare · needs attunement by a spellcaster
h:
Weight: 6 lb.

Damage: 1d6 bludgeoning (1d8 two-handed)

Properties: V

This stone and iron staff depicts a man burdened with boulders and punishment. Despite its material, it only weighs 6 pounds. While holding the staff, you have advantage on any ability check or saving throw you make to avoid falling prone. The staff has 10 charges for the following properties, which use your spell save DC.

Magic Boulder

While holding the staff, you can use an action to expend 1 of its charges to magically create and either drop or roll a boulder. If you drop the boulder, it falls at a point that you can see within 60 feet of you; each creature within 5 feet of the point must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take 5d10 bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. If you roll the boulder, you roll it in a 10-foot-wide line that's 30 feet long, originating from you; each creature within the line must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 3d10 bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. Regardless of whether you drop or roll the boulder, a prone creature has disadvantage on the saving throw, and the boulder disappears immediately afterward.

Maze

While holding the staff, you can use an action to expend 6 of its charges to cast the maze spell from it. This version of the spell shunts the creature to a special demiplane where it must push a boulder up a long, arduous hill. To escape, the target must use an action and succeed on a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check to push the boulder up the hill. It takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage each time it fails the check. When the target escapes, it suffers one level of exhaustion.

The staff regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the staff rusts, crumbles into stone dust and is destroyed.

This roll of magic red tape is covered in tiny arcane scrawlings and is slick with snail slime. The tape is 1 inch wide, and there is 50 feet of tape in the roll. You can use an action to apply a 5-foot length of tape to a solid surface (such as a floor or a wall) within your reach. When you do, you can extend the tape in additional 5-foot segments by moving in a line alongside it as part of this action.

The tape creates an invisible 10-foot-tall barrier perpendicular to the surface it's applied to. A creature that willingly attempts to cross a barrier created by slowdown tape for the first time on a turn must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature must spend 15 feet of movement to cross it.

The tape remains magical for 24 hours or until it's removed, at which point it loses its magic. A creature can use an action to remove a 5-foot length of tape within its reach by succeeding on a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check. Alternatively, dealing 10 slashing damage to the tape renders a 10-foot length of it nonmagical (5 feet on either side of the slash).

Perpetually covered in a thin layer of industrial soot, this sturdy greatcoat can double as a suit of +2 studded leather when worn without other armor beneath it. Regardless, you have resistance to fire and poison damage while wearing the greatcoat. Hidden vents line the coat and periodically belch out waste from the surrounding air: you are immune to the effects of harmful gases and vapors (such as cloudkill and stinking cloud effects, inhaled poisons, and the breath weapons of some dragons).

The coat has 5 charges for the following properties, and it regains 1d3 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While the coat has at least 1 remaining charge, its hem billows softly, as if by a dramatic breeze. You must be wearing the coat to use its properties, which use a save DC of 17.

Fumigate

As a bonus action, you can expend 1 of the coat's charges to duplicate the effects of the misty step spell from it. When you do, a cloud of thick fumes heavily obscures the area you left in a 10-foot-radius sphere, centered on a point within 5 feet of your original space. The fumes dissipate at the start of your next turn.

Steam Burst

As an action, you can expend 2 of the coat's charges to release a wave of powerful steam. Each creature within 20 feet of you (other than yourself) must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d6 fire damage and is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't pushed. Being underwater doesn't grant resistance against this damage.

Venomous Haze

As an action, you can expend 3 of the coat's charges to duplicate the effects of the cloudkill spell, centered on a point within 5 feet of you. This version of the spell doesn't require your concentration, and it creates a 30-foot-radius sphere of fog, instead of its normal size. It remains fixed on the point for the duration or until it's dispersed by wind. You can see normally within the cloud created by this spell.

m: Wondrous item · Rare · needs attunement by a spellcaster
h:
This curled leather hat rests securely atop your head, as if held in place by a magically viscous force. It has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing it, you can use an action to expend 1 of its charges to cast the slow spell from it, using your spell save DC.

Slow Shell

While wearing the hat, you gain a +1 bonus to AC if you're either concentrating on a slow spell or if you haven't moved since the start of your previous turn; this bonus is not cumulative.

Weight: 6 lb.

Armour Class: 2

This magic shield hums like a bell when struck with magical force. Whenever you make a saving throw against a spell or magical effect while holding the shield, you gain a +2 bonus to the roll if the spell or effect deals damage.

Arcane Overshield

When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell or other magical effect, you can use your reaction to take no damage from the spell (if it would normally deal half as much damage) and gain 1d10 + 10 temporary hit points. You must be holding the shield. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Weight: 3 lb.

Damage: 1d6 piercing (1d8 two-handed)

Properties: T, V

This spear is made from magical, intertwined willow branches. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The spear has 6 charges and regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn. Once per turn when you make an attack with the spear and miss, you can expend 1 of its charges to use one of the following properties, based on the type of attack you made.

Melee

If you made a melee attack with the spear, one of its willow branches lashes outward at the target to strike it. Reroll the attack roll; you must use the new result.

Thrown

If you made a ranged attack with the spear, each creature within 10 feet of the target (including the initial target) must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 + 2 piercing damage, as splinters and whiplike branches lash outward from the spear.

After using either property, the lashing branches fall to the ground and begin to take root, eventually growing into a normal willow tree.

m: Rod · Legendary · needs attunement by a cleric or druid
h:
The top of this wooden rod cradles a floating droplet of amber at its center. The rod itself is a splinter of the great world tree, Yggdrasil. While holding it, you are always under the effects of the barkskin spell, and whenever you deal damage with one of your cleric or druid cantrips, you can roll one additional damage die of the same kind and add it to the total. The rod can be used as a magic club that's always under the effects of shillelagh. It has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn.

Spells

While holding the rod, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: aura of life (2 charges), commune with nature (3 charges), locate animals or plants (trees only; no charges), plane shift (5 charges), speak with plants (trees only; 1 charge), transport via plants (4 charges), tree stride (1 charge), or wall of thorns (4 charges). This version of tree stride doesn't require your concentration, but it ends after you move through a tree with it.

Treant Form

While holding the rod, you can use an action to expend 7 of its charges to transform into a treant, as if by the polymorph spell, except you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores while transformed. This version of the treant doesn't have the Animate Trees action. The effect lasts for up to 12 hours. You can end the effect early using an action or if you're reduced to 0 hit points. While transformed, you are always under the effects of the aura of life spell, and any friendly creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of you gains 1d10 temporary hit points. You can reduce the number of charges you need to expend to transform in this way by 2 if you also expend a use of either your Channel Divinity or Wild Shape as part of using this property (no action required).

m: Melee weapon · Legendary · needs attunement by a sorcerer or wizard
