Damage: 1d6 bludgeoning (1d8 two-handed)

Properties: V

This staff has a series of narrow openings at its top through which threads of magic visibly flow. It can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff that grants a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. While holding the staff, you also gain a +1 bonus to your spell save DC, spell attack bonus, AC, and any saving throw you make.

When you cast a spell of 3rd level or higher using a spell slot and are holding the staff, threads of lingering energy wrap around the staff. The number of threads is equal to the level of the expended spell slot divided by 3 (rounded down). You can have up to 3 threads at a time, which remain until they're expended or until you finish a long rest. Until then, whenever you would expend a spell slot while holding the staff, you can instead expend a number of threads from the staff equal to the spell's level; if the spell has a casting time of 1 action, you can cast it using a bonus action instead. Regardless, treat a spell cast in this way as though it were cast with a spell slot, except that it doesn't generate any threads.

In addition, if you hit a target with the staff, it deals an extra 1d6 force damage for each thread it has.

Weight: 3 lb.

Damage: 1d8 slashing (1d10 two-handed)

Properties: V

This weapon appears as a silver katana hilt. It functions as a sun blade, except that its bonus to attack and damage rolls is +3. This weapon is said to have been the inspiration for the first sun blade, but its craftsmanship remains unmatched even millennia later. Its blade is made of pure starlight, and its edge is the breadth of a ray of light. The blade was first forged by an archfey who managed to contain the shimmering starlight—by complete happenstance—by correctly guessing the light's true name as it streaked towards the horizon as a shooting star.

Starlight Arc

When you take the Attack action on your turn using this weapon, you can forgo the first attack you make to cause the blade to emit an arc of light, which travels until it reaches the nearest creature to you in a 30-foot cone; if multiple creatures in the cone are equidistant from you (such as a pair of creatures standing next to each other), it reaches each of them simultaneously. Make a single melee attack with the blade, using that attack roll against each target the arc of light reached. On a hit, a target takes an extra 1d8 radiant damage from the attack, and any illusions on it are magically ended. Hit or miss, the arc of light dissipates after the attack, and any other creatures within the cone are unaffected.

Sunburst

You can use an action while holding the katana to cast the sunburst spell from it (save DC 15). This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

Sentience

The starfire katana is a sentient chaotic good weapon with an Intelligence of 8, a Wisdom of 13, and a Charisma of 17. It has hearing and darkvision out to a range of 120 feet. The weapon communicates telepathically with its wielder and can speak, read, and understand Celestial, Common, and Sylvan.

Personality

The starfire katana is interested in the goings-on of the Inner Planes. It sees the endless push and pull of forces, especially in the Material Plane, like a living and unpredictable ocean tide. Its personality is bound to the light it emits, and it has spent millennia simply careening through the stars. As a result, even the mundane happenings of civilization can still fascinate the sword. When given a choice, it prefers to steer the tide against the forces of evil, but it acknowledges fully that "evil" is a matter of perspective and time, of which it has much.

This glass lamp is inky and dark inside. When left outside after dusk, a number of glimmering stars appear within the lamp. The number of stars is equal to the number of hours the lamp was left outside, up to a maximum of 8. While holding the lamp, it emits dim light out to a range of 20 feet, provided it has any stars within it. You can use an action while holding the lamp to speak its command word, sending out a number of floating lights from the lamp of your choice, up to the number of remaining stars. Sending a light removes a star from the lamp; each light emits dim light in a 10-foot radius. Choose a point for each light to hover in that you can see, up to 60 feet away from you, where it remains for 1 hour or until you wave the lamp through it (provided you're within reach of the point). Waving the lamp through the light extinguishes it and returns a star to the lamp, up to its maximum.

This clump of soft fleece feels numbing and electrical to the touch. When you cast a spell that uses fleece as a material component that isn't consumed in the casting (such as major image, minor illusion, phantasmal force, or silent image), you can choose to use this fleece to enhance the spell. The fleece must be on your person. When a spell is cast in this way, choose one of the following benefits:

  • A creature that uses an action to interact and come into physical contact with the spell must first make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature ceases trying to interact with the spell (potentially delaying it recognizing the spell as an illusion) and can't make opportunity attacks until the start of its next turn.
  • When the spell ends, you can choose for it to release a small blast of electricity. Each creature within 10 feet of the spell when it ends in this way must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d10 lightning damage and is stunned until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't stunned.

Each time the fleece is used, roll a d4. On a 1, the fleece loses its electrical charge and becomes nonmagical.

This stick resembles a crooked, wooden finger. As a result, it's earned the colloquial nickname of a hag's finger. You can use an action while holding this stick to shake it at up to five visible targets that you can see within 60 feet of you. When you do, those targets become outlined with an illusory glow until the end of the turn, making them immediately discernible; this glow is only visible to you and other creatures of your choice that are within 10 feet of you.

This peculiar crochet hook is actually a wand cherished by a matronly witch. It also functions as a set of weaver's tools and creates its own yarn while crocheting or knitting with it; you choose the color and texture of the yarn, which is nonmagical.

The wand has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the wand, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to target a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must then succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be transformed into a Tiny plushlike version of itself. While transformed, the creature cannot speak, move, or take actions that would require it to physically move; it also has an AC of 10, and it automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws. A creature can choose to fail the saving throw to resist being transformed.

A creature remains transformed in this way for an amount of time based on the charges expended: 1 (1 minute), 2 (10 minutes), or 3 (1 hour). The effect ends early if your concentration on the effect ends (as if you were concentrating on a spell), or if the creature takes any damage, at which point any damage dealt carries over to its normal form.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement by a monk
h:
These dusty leather footwraps are stitched with a geographic pattern. While wearing them, you gain the following benefits.

Step of Stone

You gain tremorsense out to a range of 10 feet, and difficult terrain composed of earth or stone doesn't cost you extra movement. When you expend a ki point to use your Step of the Wind, the range of this tremorsense increases to 30 feet until the start of your next turn.

Stone Blow

When you expend a ki point to use your Flurry of Blows as a bonus action, you can replace any of the unarmed strikes you make as part of it with a special attack. This attack summons an earthen slab from the ground below a target that you can see within 60 feet of you, striking the target with unyielding force before returning to the ground. Treat the attack as if it were a normal unarmed strike, except it ignores half and three-quarters cover. If you use your Stunning Strike on an unarmed strike made in this way, the attack also deals an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage.

Stone Defense

When you expend a ki point to use your Patient Defense as a bonus action, you can choose to grant yourself resistance to piercing and slashing damage until the start of your next turn, instead of its normal effects.

Once the ribbon has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

These cups are a favorite of tricksters, illusionists, and gamblers. They're made of a soft porcelain with a pleasing blue pattern, and they typically come in sets of four.

While holding one of the cups, you can speak its command word to cause the cup you're holding to magically switch places with another one that you can see, provided it's within 10 feet of you. The cups switch instantly, including anything contained within them. A creature can detect the switch with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. Other differences in the cups, such as what's contained within, may make it more obvious that there was a switch. Once two cups have been switched, neither of those cups can be switched again until the next dawn.

The cups' command word is unique in that it's an extremely common word (typically "Well," "Good," or "See" in Common) but only activates if the holder is also gently tapping the cup (such as conversationally or thoughtfully).

m: Melee weapon · Legendary · needs attunement by a creature of lawful alignment
h:
Weight: 3 lb.

Damage: 1d8 slashing (1d10 two-handed)

Properties: V

This regal sword's guard and handle are designed in the likeness of a judge's scale. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and you can't be frightened while holding it. The sword has 8 charges, and it regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn.

Burden of Damocles

While holding the sword, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 of its charges to curse a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. A creature cursed in this way sees a phantasmal copy of the sword of Damocles floating in the air, just above its head; the sword is invisible, except to you and the cursed creature. As part of the curse, choose one of the following triggering conditions: the target deals damage to another creature, it forces a creature to make a saving throw, it tells a deliberate lie, or it knowingly breaks a law (GM's discretion). The creature knows what the triggering condition is. When the condition is met, the phantasmal sword becomes visible and drops, forcing the creature to make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. The creature takes 4d10 + 3 force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The curse ends after 24 hours have passed or when its triggering condition is met, at which point you magically learn the outcome. If you use this property of the sword to curse a creature already cursed in this way, you can choose to either replace the previous curse with a new one or increase the damage dealt by the curse by 2d10, up to a maximum of 8d10 + 3 force damage.

This canvas bag has a pattern resembling the bronchial airways embroidered on either side. At its top is a metal valve. The bag holds 10 minutes of air and regains 1d10 used minutes daily at dawn. You can use an action to inhale 1 or more minutes' worth of air from the bag. Unless you speak or otherwise exhale, you don't have to breathe again for that number of minutes.

This golden throne is covered in lion-like embellishments, complete with feet, claws, and mane. It doubles as a single golden lion figurine of wondrous power, except that you must touch it when you speak its first command word to cause it to become a lion, and it can't be used again until 3 days have passed, instead of 7.

You can speak its second command word as an action to make the throne stand slightly taller. The chair continues to stand in this way until you or another creature sit in it. If you move more than 30 feet from the throne, it follows you until it is within 30 feet of you, using a walking speed of 30 feet. It takes the shortest route to do so. If prevented from moving, the chair sinks to its normal resting height and becomes inactive. While sitting on the throne, you can use an action to command it to carry you a distance up to its walking speed, and you have advantage on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks you make to interact with any kind of cat, even if it isn't domesticated.

Inside this book are pages filled with strange musings and detailed illustrations of impossible staircases and doorways. While this book is set in a bookcase against a wall, you can use an action to tip it toward you and speak its command word. When you do, the bookcase shudders and slides into the wall behind it, revealing a magical passageway. This passageway connects to another wall of your choice within the same structure, provided it's within 300 feet of you and you're familiar with the other wall; the passageway is up to 5 feet wide and 8 feet tall. The passageway magically connects the two walls, creating a structurally sound opening between them that's always 20 feet long (even if it can't be rationalized within the space). You choose whether the passageway's exit is left open or is covered by an unlocked door. The book then topples onto the bookshelf or into your hand (your choice), and this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

The passageway remains for 1 hour. When the passageway disappears, the bookcase slides back out of the wall, and any creatures or objects still inside the passageway are safely ejected to the nearest unoccupied space outside the bookcase.

This hefty tome is filled with a thousand ancient pages of incomprehensible text from multiple dead languages. Reading the book serves no purpose, as its texts are indecipherable even with the aid of magic. A warlock gains a +3 bonus to any Intelligence check or Intelligence saving throw it makes while the book is on its person.

Holding the book fills a person with the same sense of dread as standing on the edge of a cliff, which a creature holding the book can use an action to mentally jump from. When it does, that creature must make a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 6d8 psychic damage and is stunned for 1 minute. This damage can't be reduced in any way, and the condition can't be prevented or ended early. On a success, the creature then gains the benefits of either the contact other plane or legend lore spell (its choice each time); it doesn't make the saving throw again as part of the contact other plane spell in this way. The save DC for this property increases by 1 each subsequent time it's used after the first, resetting to 15 again daily at dawn.

Curse

This book is cursed, which can only be detected by a legend lore spell. A creature that rolls a 1 on the saving throw when using the book's properties becomes cursed by it. Only a greater restoration spell or similar magic can end this curse. Each day at dawn, a creature cursed in this way suffers a cumulative -1 penalty to any Intelligence check or Intelligence saving throw it makes. If the penalty drops to -10, the creature's Intelligence score is reduced to 1, and it is incapacitated until the curse is ended.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement by a bard
h:
This mandolin excels at bestowing overwhelming sadness and distress. Whenever you deal psychic damage while holding the mandolin, you can reroll any 1 or 2 you roll on the damage die; you must use the new result. A creature that attempts to play the instrument without being attuned to it must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or take 2d4 psychic damage.

Inspire Ruin

While holding the mandolin, you can use an action to expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration to cast the dissonant whispers or hideous laughter spell from it, using your spell save DC. When cast in this way, the target makes its saving throw against the spell with disadvantage.

Melody of Despair

While holding the mandolin, you can use an action to begin playing a sorrowful melody. You can continue playing until your concentration on it ends (as if concentrating on a spell), up to a maximum of 10 minutes, or until you're no longer holding the mandolin. For the duration, any hostile creature that enters a space within 30 feet of you for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC; a creature automatically succeeds on the saving throw if it can't hear the melody. A creature can only make this save once per turn. On a failed save, the creature becomes wracked with despair: its speed is halved, it has vulnerability to psychic damage (unless it already has immunity to it), and it deals only half damage with weapon attacks that use Strength. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn unless you also expend two uses of your Bardic Inspiration when beginning to play the melody.

Weight: 6 lb.

Armour Class: 2

This shield once belonged to a traitorous knight who was burned for his treason. While holding the shield, you have resistance to necrotic damage.

Damned Rebuke

When you take damage from a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you and are holding the shield, you can use your reaction to cast the hellish rebuke spell from the shield (2nd-level version; save DC 15). You choose whether the spell's damage type is fire or necrotic each time you cast it. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn or until you take 10 or more damage from a single friendly source while holding the shield.

Curse

This shield is cursed, and attuning to it extends the curse to you. While you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the shield, and you have disadvantage on saving throws against spells and effects created by friendly creatures.

This fist-sized stone figurine can be used to create a trench in natural ground, such as dirt, sand, or unworked stone. You can use an action to place the figurine on the ground at a point within 5 feet of you and speak its command word. A four-foot-deep trench then appears in the ground, provided it's eligible; the trench is composed of up to six 5-foot-square segments. Each segment must be contiguous with at least one other segment, and they must form a straight line on the surface of the ground originating from the figurine. The trench can't extend underneath a structure or similar obstacle: its surface must remain exposed.

The trench remains until the figurine is removed from the ground (no action required); the figurine remains above the trench unless each space on the ground surrounding the point is part of the line. When this happens, anything within the trench is lifted upward as the ground fills in beneath it. Once the trench disappears, this property of the figurine can't be used again until the next dawn.

A Medium or Small creature within the trench has three-quarters cover against ranged attacks made from outside the trench; if such a creature is prone, it instead has total cover against such attacks. Especially tall creatures may need to crouch in order to gain the trench's cover against ranged attacks (GM's discretion), whereas Tiny creatures may be completely obscured from outside view within the trench.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
This circlet has 9 charges and regains 1d4 + 5 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing it, you have a collection of invisible fox tails behind you equal to the circlet's number of remaining charges. Only you and creatures that can see invisible objects (such as a creature benefiting from see invisibility or truesight) can see the tails. Whenever you're hit by an attack, you can roll one or more d6s, to a maximum of the number of fox tails you have remaining (no action required). If at least one of the dice rolls a 4 or higher, the attack misses you, as it's intercepted by a fox tail. The circlet then lose a number of charges equal to the number of dice that rolled a 4 or higher. If an attack misses you in this way, you can immediately use your reaction to make you and anything you're wearing or carrying invisible until the end of the turn, and you can immediately move up to half your speed.

If you're a rogue and know the mage hand cantrip, you can use an action while wearing the circlet to expend 5 of its charges to cast the arcane hand spell from it. This version of the spell doesn't require your concentration.

Weight: 4 lb.

Damage: 1d6 piercing (1d8 two-handed)

Properties: T, V

This metal trident is covered in sharp icicles. It has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. It deals an extra 1d6 cold damage to any target it hits.

Once per turn when you hit or miss with a ranged attack using the trident, you can choose to expend 1 of its charges to cause a dazzling flash of ice and light to erupt from the trident. Each hostile creature within 10 feet of the target must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw; the target of the attack has disadvantage on the save. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d10 cold damage and 1d10 radiant damage and is blinded until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't blinded. In addition, friendly creatures within the effect's area gain resistance to cold damage for the next minute. The trident then crystalizes into solid ice, shatters, and reappears in a flash of light in your open hand or at your feet (your choice).

This string of carved bone figurines depicts five classic beasts found in the icy winter tundra. It has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. As an action, you can speak the string's command word while touching a figurine to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast the polymorph spell from it, targeting only yourself and transforming into the creature associated with it: elk (1 charge), owl (1 charge), polar bear (3 charges), saber-toothed tiger (3 charges), or wolf (2 charges). This version of polymorph allows you to retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores while transformed, and it grants you resistance to cold damage for the duration of the spell.

If you expend the last charge from the string, roll a d10. On a 1, the touched charm breaks, falling from the string and removing the option to transform into that creature in this way.

Weight: 2 lb.

Damage: 1d6 piercing

Properties: A, 2H

Also called a lover's bow or Cupid's bow, this bow features two bowstrings that resonate while they touch. This magic weapon uses 2d4 for its damage dice, instead of a d6. If the two d4s roll the same number, the target of the attack must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn or until it takes any damage. If the charm ends early as a result of you dealing damage to the target, the target takes an extra 2d4 psychic damage as its momentary infatuation is shattered.

Charming Arrows

This bow has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can use an action while holding the bow to expend 1 of its charges to cast the charm person spell from it (save DC 15). Alternatively, you can forgo making an attack with the bow to expend 1 of its charges to cast the spell instead: when you do, you fire an illusory, harmless arrow from the bow at the target, which must be within 30 feet of you. This version of the spell allows you to choose a creature other than yourself to be the one the target is charmed by; the other creature must be within 10 feet of the target. A creature that's already charmed by you has disadvantage on the saving throw against the spell when cast from the bow.
